jobs.description:
Company: Siemens Industry, Inc.

Location: 1000 Deerfield Parkway, Buffalo Grove, IL 60089

Position Title: Customer Services Project Manager

Salary $133,182 - $150,144 / Year

Hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, 40 Hours/Week

Summary of Duties: Manage projects from inception to completion, ensuring safety, budget, schedule, quality, and performance objectives are met. Communicate effectively with team members, stakeholders, and management, providing regular updates and managing customer expectations throughout the project lifecycle. Identify, assign, and manage project resources, including engineering, field personnel, vendors, and 3rd party services. Proactively identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and monitor/control 3rd party vendors to ensure contract adherence. Track project budget, schedule completion, and perform monthly revenue forecasting. Review and understand contractual obligations, manage change orders, and participate in vendor negotiations. Develop project execution plans like quality and testing plans, schedules, and risk registers. Implement recovery plans to address performance issues. Collaborate with internal/external teams and clients to develop site schedules, maintain client relationships, and provide feedback to improve project offerings. Project types include: Installation and commission, turnkey design-build, engineer, procure, construct (EPC), power system studies, maintenance outage testing and electrical system emergency response/disaster recovery, electrical retrofit managing teams of field service engineers as well as 3rd party suppliers, consultants, and contractors. Product types include: Low and medium voltage air insulated switchgear, medium voltage gas insulated switchgear and switches, air and liquid filled transformers, motor control center, medium voltage contractors, integrate e-house electrical solution systems, battery systems, electrical cable systems and busways, cable, connectors, and supporting systems. Up to 25% domestic travel required. Remote work permitted.

Qualifications: The position requires a Bachelor’s degree in Management, Business, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field and five (5) years of experience in the job offered or as a Project Coordinator, Project Engineer, Contracts Manager, Field Service Engineer, Field Service Technician, or an acceptable alternate occupation. The position requires five (5) years of experience with the following skills: Direct Project Management experience within construction, including in electrical distribution; Experience presenting complex issues to multilevel audiences and communicating to internal and external stakeholders; Direct Project Management Experience: risk management, budget management, field personnel management, schedule management, financial reporting, change order negotiation, engineering drawing review, safety protocols, stakeholder management, project planning, and progress evaluations. The position requires four (4) years of experience with the following skills: Experience with design or installation of medium or low voltage distribution; Experience with datacenter construction projects. Up to 25% domestic travel required. Remote work permitted.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Description & Requirements

AESC is looking to add a Project Manager to our team.

Full-Time
Remote

About AESC US LLC

AESC is an exciting, newly created global organization committed to solving the challenges of a sustainable future and becoming the leading supplier of full-value-chain battery solutions. Our lithium-ion batteries can be found in nearly one million electric vehicles worldwide and have a stellar safety record of zero-critical issues. AESC US is leading the way in battery technology. We design and manufacture EV battery technology for various electric vehicles and equipment. We are working hard towards unlocking the full potential of sustainable energy and climate change mitigation. We will continue to build upon our successes and expand into new markets and industries, producing innovative and competitive products and technologies that advance the goal of a zero-carbon emission future. AESC is headquartered in Japan and has battery manufacturing locations in Japan, UK, China, and the U.S.

AESC Mission

Our mission is to solve the challenges for a sustainable future. Together, we can make a meaningful impact.

About The Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Project Manager to support the execution of utility-scale energy storage and infrastructure projects. This role will focus on project administration, scheduling, documentation, and internal cross-team coordination to ensure smooth delivery of complex projects. The Project Manager will work closely with sales managers, engineering teams, and external stakeholders to maintain project momentum from initiation through completion.

Project Management

What You Will Do

Serve as the central point of contact for project documentation, scheduling, and reporting.
Support sales managers and project managers in tracking milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.
Coordinate internal resources and external partners to ensure timely execution of project tasks.
Maintain accurate project records, including meeting minutes, action items, and progress reports.
Assist with preparation of project proposals, RFP/RFQ responses, and client-facing documentation.
Monitor project timelines and budgets, escalating risks or delays to senior management.
Facilitate communication between cross-functional teams (engineering, procurement, sales, and services).
Support compliance with organizational standards, safety requirements, and quality assurance processes.

Technical Management

Lead remote commissioning activities for energy storage systems, including system configuration, functional testing, and performance validation.
Act as the technical authority during commissioning, guiding and directing the commissioning team to ensure successful project execution.
Perform and oversee technical service work, including troubleshooting, diagnostics, and repairs for energy storage systems.
Provide advanced technical support for service issues and collaborate with engineering teams to resolve complex challenges.
Prepare and maintain detailed commissioning and service documentation, including test reports and maintenance records.
Ensure compliance with safety standards, quality requirements, and regulatory guidelines during all commissioning and service activities.
Offer technical training and mentorship to commissioning and service team members.

Qualifications

What You Need

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).
2–4 years of project coordination, project support, or operations experience; exposure to utility-scale energy, infrastructure, or construction projects preferred.
Familiarity with project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid).
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Proficiency with project management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana, Jira) and Microsoft Office.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey technical and commercial information clearly.
Self-driven, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment

What is “Nice to Have”?

Knowledge of energy storage systems, renewable energy, or large-scale infrastructure projects.
Understanding of permitting, interconnection, and regulatory processes.
Experience supporting EPCs, utilities, IPPs, or project developers.
Familiarity with CRM platforms and project tracking systems.

What We Offer

Welcome to AESC, supporting our state-of-the-art Gigafactories, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. At AESC, we offer a comprehensive compensation package. In addition, we provide a range of valuable benefits, such as 401K, and health insurance. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission of changing the world.

An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment
Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts
401K with company match
Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available)
Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays
Short term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid)
Tuition reimbursement
Competitive base salary with performance-based incentives.
Opportunity to contribute to large-scale energy transition projects impacting grid reliability and decarbonization.
Hands-on exposure to complex, high-value infrastructure projects.
Comprehensive training in project management methodologies and energy storage technologies.
Career growth opportunities within project management, operations, or commercial functions.
Comprehensive benefits package including [health insurance, retirement plan, PTO, etc.].

Application Process

Even if you don't meet every requirement listed, if you believe this role suits you well, we encourage you to apply. Your application gives us the opportunity to learn more about you and explore potential fits within our team.

Following the submission of your application, we are committed to providing timely responses to all applicants, though response times may vary depending on the volume of submissions. If you do not receive an immediate response, please rest assured that this in no way reflects on the quality of your candidacy. Your application will be retained in our files, and we may reach out to you for future roles that align with your skills and interests. As our organization experiences rapid growth, we appreciate your patience in this process. We are actively working each day to enhance our application procedures to ensure a smoother and more efficient experience for all applicants. Thank you for your understanding and enthusiasm for joining our dynamic team.
Equal Employment Opportunity

At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable otherwise qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Ability to sit for extended periods of time.
Ability to read, write, speak, hear; stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach and lift with hands and arms frequently throughout the day.
Required to occasionally lift, push, pull and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally required to lift, push, pull and/or move up to 35 pounds.

Work Environment

The work environment is primarily an automated manufacturing plant with a concrete floor and is characterized by some temperature extremes, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. The individual must be able to perform all essential functions as appropriate on the plant floor, in meetings, and with employees, management, customers and suppliers.

Candidate must perform the essential duties and responsibilities with or without reasonable accommodation efficiently and accurately, and without causing significant safety threat to self or others. Overview

When you think of InComm Payments, think of Innovative Payments Technology. We were founded over 30 years ago and continue to be a pioneer in the payment (FinTech) industry. Since our inception, we have grown to be a team of over 3,000 employees in 35 countries around the world. We own over 400 global technical patents and a network that includes over 525,000 points of retail distribution that points to our industry expertise.

InComm Payments works with the most recognized and valued brands in the world, and we are partnered with most of the world’s leading merchants. InComm Payments is highly focused on our people and their growth, and we work hard to make a career at InComm Payments meaningful and rewarding. We value innovation, quality, passion, integrity, and responsibility in all that we do, and we are looking for great people to join our team as we move forward towards a very bright future.

You can learn more about InComm Payments by visiting our Website or connecting with us on LinkedIn, YouTube, Twitter, Facebook, or Instagram.

About This Opportunity

The International Implementations team supports Sales, Marketing, IT and Operational efforts in a diverse and challenging global business environment.

As an International Implementations Manager (IM), you will be responsible for managing the delivery of multiple small to medium-size projects which require the ability to lead and influence project stakeholders. On larger and more complex strategic projects, the IM may participate as a consultant or subject matter expert in support of traditional IT Project Management resources. The IM may also be responsible for operational management of 3rd Party Processors and InComm Retailers as it relates to Product Implementations.

When supporting Product Implementations and/or Partner Integrations, it is the IM’s responsibility to conduct a wide variety of Project Management activities across multiple internal and external groups to deliver. Typical projects will include high-level, complex requests with high priority and strategic need. IMs are also expected to lead, mentor, and train less seasoned staff to aid in continual improvement and education efforts. IMs are expected to oversee activities to facilitate project workflow in a timely manner and to break down barriers when necessary to assure the needs of InComm Retailers and Partners are met. Project efforts are consistent in approach and are comprised of many repeatable and process driven tasks.

The role will also deliver documentation and process improvements which increase efficiency in the way InComm executes and drives Partner satisfaction. This role will provide a consolidated, single point of service and communication regarding product implementations internally and externally.

Responsibilities

Major Responsibilities:

Full E2E Accountability for International Implementations
Coordination/Assistance with Partner/Retailer Integrations
Responsible for Project Pre-Planning, Milestone Tracking, Execution, Oversight, Wrap-Up, and Lessons Learned Activities, as Required

Build and Maintain Analytical Dashboards and/or Automated Process Flows using MS Office O365 Toolsets including CoPilot and other Generative AI/LLM Technologies, as Required
Distribution of Communications to All Stakeholders for Assigned Projects
Support Internal Support Teams and act as Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Resolution of Internal Trouble Tickets, as Required
Coordinate and Manage All Special Projects or Miscellaneous Assignments, as Required
Ensure All Milestone Updates are Timely, Accurate, and Informative
Utilize Scheduling and Forecasting Toolsets to Reduce Escalations & Increase Throughput
Build Rapport with Business Teams Globally to Enable Effective Communication and Collaboration
Promote Idea Generation and Collaboration with Cross-Functional Teams
Track and Log Issues, Roadblocks, and Highlights to be reviewed in Search of Continuous Improvement
Spearhead Efforts to Maintain and Regularly Update on Retailer and Partner Level Implementation Requirements
Assist Leadership in Forecasting Regional Product Implementation Pipeline
Act as SME in Various Areas of Business
Identify System Updates and Configurations, as Required
Ensure Timely & Accurate Delivery of Projects/Products
Examine and Document Business Processes Where Relevant
All Other Duties Assigned or Required

Qualifications

Qualities / Skills:

Strong Technical and Business Acumen
Understanding of Transaction Processing
Ability to Communicate Technical and Business Requirements Effectively Between Sales and IT
Self-Directed, Detail Oriented, and Decisive
Willingness to Take Initiative and Drive Problems Toward Solutions
Ability to Influence Others and Develop Strong Business Relationships
Adaptable/Flexible & Well-Organized
Strong Problem Solving, Troubleshooting, and Analytical Skills
Ability to Delegate Tasks and Manage to Completion
Excellent Time Management and Prioritization Skills
Strong Written and Oral Communication

Ability to Work in a Fast-Paced and Highly Seasonal Environment

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Information Technology, or Related Field, or Equivalent Work Experience Required
1+ years of Experience Working in Account Management, Project Management and/or Product Implementations in a Relevant Industry and/or Setting
1+ years in Software or Technical IT Environment
Experience in Delivering Communications and Reports to Cross-Functional Management Teams
Excellent Project Management Skills to Successfully Lead and Manage Multiple Complex Projects Simultaneously

jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Project Manager (Data Centers)
to join us in Houston, TX.
The following locations will also be considered: San Diego, CA, New York, NY, Houston, TX, Portland, OR and Seattle, WA
. This position can be offered remotely.

As demand for AI, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure accelerates, our clients are developing some of the world's largest, most complex, and most power-intensive facilities. In this role, you will help deliver the electrical infrastructure that enables next-generation data center campuses—projects requiring hundreds of megawatts of power and unprecedented levels of planning, engineering, and coordination. You will work across the full project lifecycle, playing a key role in delivering critical infrastructure for some of the industry's most prominent clients.

What makes this opportunity unique is the breadth of collaboration across WSP's global organization. You will work alongside top experts in their field to solve highly complex infrastructure challenges. This multidisciplinary environment provides exposure to the full range of technical and strategic considerations required to successfully develop large-scale data center campuses. You will contribute to the planning and design of substations, transmission interconnections, and site electrical infrastructure while supporting fast-paced projects that demand innovation, technical excellence, and strong collaboration.

If you're energized by large-scale infrastructure projects, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and want to help shape the future of digital infrastructure, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact while accelerating your career on some of the most significant power delivery projects being developed today.

Provides technical project supervision and guidance in managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of critical high-voltage infrastructure for data center projects in alignment with WSP’s core values and contractual commitments. Tasks include responsibility for overall performance of distribution system and grid modernization projects of moderate size/complexity and/or local/regional scope. Oversight includes financial performance, technical execution, client satisfaction, quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC), safety, and schedule adherence.

Ensures that responsibilities throughout the full project lifecycle (feasibility, engineering design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout) are executed in compliance with corporate standards, regulatory requirements (e.g., NERC, IEEE, NEC), and utility industry best practices.

Your Impact

Lead and oversee cross-functional teams delivering power distribution and utility engineering projects, ensuring execution of design and construction deliverables.
Manage multiple concurrent projects involving distribution lines, feeders, and grid infrastructure upgrades, including budgets, schedule, cost control, and resource allocation.
Develop and manage project scopes, cost estimates, schedules, and resource plans for utility capital improvement programs and distribution projects.
Build and maintain Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) aligned with engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) project delivery models.
Ensure compliance with utility standards, environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and safety protocols (OSHA, utility HSE standards).
Participate in proposal development, RFP responses, and business development efforts within the power & energy market.
Perform margin analysis, risk assessments, and contingency planning for power delivery projects.
Coordinate contract negotiations, client presentations, and stakeholder meetings with utilities, municipalities, and regulatory agencies.
Develop and maintain project plans including PMP, Safety Plans, Risk Management Plans, and QA/QC procedures.
Collaborate with engineering teams specializing in all aspects of distribution design.
Partner with Project Accounting to manage financials including forecasting, earned value management (EVM), and profitability tracking.
Lead efforts in change management, scope control, and claims mitigation.
Coordinate with technical managers on staffing for overhead and underground distribution projects.
Ensure adherence to health, safety, and environmental (HSE) standards, escalating issues when necessary.
Provide reporting to clients and leadership on project performance, risks, schedule, and budget status.
Manage project closeout activities, including lessons learned and continuous improvement for future projects.
Stay current on power industry trends, grid resilience, distributed energy resources (DER), and electrification initiatives.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or related field.
7+ years of experience managing projects in power distribution, transmission & distribution (T&D), or utility engineering environments.
Proven experience delivering feeder, distribution line, or grid modernization projects.

Company Description

Moveworks
is the Agentic AI Assistant platform that empowers the entire workforce.

Our platform enables employees to converse with all of their business systems through natural language to quickly find answers and automate tasks. Powered by the world's most advanced LLMs, our proprietary models, and a sophisticated Agentic AI platform, we're transforming how work gets done by allowing AI to take initiative, streamline complex workflows, and continuously learn and adapt.

Moveworks is trusted by over 5.5 million employees at more than 350 of the world’s largest companies, including 10% of the Fortune 500, to automate everyday tasks and streamline business operations. Recognized on the Forbes Cloud 100 and AI 50 lists, Moveworks was also named one of Fast Company’s 2025 Most Innovative Companies and Inc’s Best in Business, in the Best in Innovation category. Moveworks was also recognized at Microsoft’s 2025 Partner of the Year and in 2024, received the AI Breakthrough Award.

In December 2025, Moveworks was acquired by ServiceNow, marking a pivotal milestone in our journey to create a single front door to work for all business systems. By combining ServiceNow’s leading workflow automation with Moveworks’ Reasoning Engine and natural language capabilities, we deliver the AI platform for every person and every workflow. Built to go beyond basic summaries to deliver meaningful business impact. Together, our AI acts across enterprise systems to turn conversations into completed work.

By joining our team, you’ll be at the forefront of the AI transformation, backed by the global scale of ServiceNow and the agility of a high-growth company. We are looking for world-class talent to help us extend agentic AI to every employee across every corner of the business.

ServiceNow

It all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.

The Implementation Manager oversees the on-time, on-budget delivery of the Moveworks platform to meet the customer's desired results. Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.

Creativity with comfort running projects independently.

Diplomatic, tactful, and poised under pressure.
Bachelor's degree.

Digitas Health is the modern creative agency that takes on the biggest moments in healthcare

Purpose-built for today’s complex and evolving landscape, we partner with some of the world’s largest healthcare brands to do big things by moving faster, connecting deeper, and unlocking new possibilities at the intersection of creativity, data, technology, and empathy. —we deliver meaningful work that drives relevance, changes behavior, and creates lasting impact, always grounded in humanity, not just technology. As part of Publicis Health and Publicis Groupe
, we bring together entrepreneurial energy with the scale, stability, and depth of one of the world’s leading communications networks.

At Digitas Health, what sets us apart isn’t just who we work with, it’s how we work and how it feels to be here. Our culture attracts curious, driven people who want to make a difference and be part of something bigger.
Our teams are intentionally crafted across disciplines, perspectives, and experience levels, bringing strategy, creativity, data, and technology together from the start. We believe the best ideas come from curiosity, collaboration, and healthy debate and we expect people here to be thoughtful, engaged, and eager to shape what’s next. If you’re energized by complexity, motivated by impact, and excited to help redefine how healthcare connects with people, we’d love to meet you!

Overview

Project Managers independently lead projects across multiple workstreams, owning delivery from planning through completion while balancing scope, timing, budget, quality, and client expectations.

Project Managers bring clarity to complexity. They identify risks early, make informed decisions, manage competing priorities, and adjust plans before issues affect scope, cost, quality, or client confidence. They are trusted to own outcomes, navigate day-to-day trade-offs, and create confidence for teams, stakeholders, and clients through sound judgment and reliable execution.

As active delivery leaders, Project Managers apply strong project management, financial, and operational expertise to keep work moving forward, improve how work gets done, and strengthen delivery outcomes. They use new tools, technologies, and ways of working to improve visibility, efficiency, and delivery outcomes as client and business needs evolve.

Responsibilities

Strategy

Develop and manage project plans that establish a clear path to successful delivery across multiple workstreams.
Make day-to-day decisions that balance scope, timing, budget, quality, resource availability, and client needs.
Anticipate risks, trade-offs, and resource constraints early, adjusting plans and priorities to protect project outcomes.
Manage project scope and financial health proactively, identifying risks, evaluating options, and recommending solutions that support successful delivery and responsible business outcomes.
Lead discussions around priorities, resource needs, and delivery approaches, helping teams stay focused on the work that matters most.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, tools, and ways of working, applying changes that strengthen delivery outcomes and team effectiveness.

Delivery

Own successful delivery across multiple workstreams, ensuring work is completed on time, on budget, and at the expected level of quality.
Actively manage project scope, budgets, forecasts, timelines, and resource plans, identifying risks and opportunities early and driving solutions that support successful delivery and responsible business outcomes.
Monitor project health and delivery performance, proactively mitigating risks, addressing issues, and communicating impacts before they affect outcomes.
Manage scope changes, evolving priorities, and project constraints, helping teams understand implications, evaluate options, and move forward with clarity.
Lead cross-functional teams through delivery challenges, resolving dependencies, removing obstacles, and driving action to keep work moving forward.
Apply and evolve processes, tools, technologies, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve visibility, efficiency, execution quality, and delivery outcomes.

Knowledge

Apply project management, financial, and operational expertise to support sound delivery decisions and successful project outcomes.
Develop accurate estimates, scopes of work, budgets, forecasts, and resource plans that support effective planning and execution.
Apply financial and contractual knowledge to evaluate project health, identify risks early, and make recommendations that support responsible business outcomes.
Use project management platforms, workflow tools, and reporting to identify trends, inform decisions, and improve delivery performance.
Understand the business objectives behind the work and apply that context to delivery decisions, prioritization, and stakeholder discussions.
Evaluate and apply new tools, technologies, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve efficiency, visibility, and delivery outcomes.

Leadership

Build trust and confidence with teams, stakeholders, and clients through sound judgment, accountability, and follow-through.
Communicate project status, risks, decisions, and trade-offs clearly, distilling complex information into the key points teams and clients need to understand, so teams and clients understand what is happening, why it matters, and what comes next.
Manage client and stakeholder relationships proactively, addressing concerns early and maintaining confidence in delivery.
Own project outcomes by following issues through resolution and making the day-to-day decisions needed to keep work moving.
Bring forward practical recommendations, solutions, and next steps when teams need clarity or direction.
Use evolving tools, technologies, and ways of working to improve communication, collaboration, and delivery confidence.

Qualifications

What You Bring

3-5 years of agency, marketing, communications, healthcare, or related experience leading project delivery across multiple workstreams and stakeholders.
Strong project management and financial management skills, with the ability to balance scope, timing, budget, quality, and client needs.
Sound judgment and the confidence to make day-to-day decisions that keep work moving forward.
Strong communication and relationship management skills, with the ability to build alignment, navigate challenges, and create confidence with teams and clients.
A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to identify risks, evaluate options, and recommend a path forward.
Curiosity about new tools, technologies, and ways of working, with the ability to apply them to improve delivery outcomes.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

Additional Information

Our Publicis Groupe motto “Viva La Différence” means we’re better together, and we believe that our differences make us stronger. It means we honor and celebrate all identities, across all facets of intersectionality, and it underpins all that we do as an organization. We are focused on fostering belonging and creating equitable & inclusive experiences for all talent.

jobs.title: Strategic Pre-Sales Program Manager - Security Systems Integration
jobs.description:
Overview

Kastle is a leader in premier property technology solutions, protecting everything from commercial real estate and global enterprises to critical government facilities and life-science labs. For over 50 years, we have provided safety to tens of thousands of businesses through state-of-the-art access control, video surveillance, and identity management. What makes us exceptional is our end-to-end approach to Managed Security as a Service. Because we engineer, install, monitor, and maintain our own systems, we are fully invested in their performance. Please visit Kastle Innovation to learn more about our solutions.

As the Pre-Sales Program Manager,
you are the single point of accountability for Kastle’s most complex Regional and National accounts. You will own the entire presales cycle from initial qualification through client acceptance. While you will not be doing technical design, you will act as a project leader uniting sales, engineering, subcontractors, and operations into a cohesive winning strategy. You will ensure every proposal is backed by a defined scope, schedule, and smooth operational handoff. To thrive here, you need strong program management experience and the executive presence to engage directly with ownership groups, developers, and enterprise clients.

Our success is driven by the combination of advanced technology and talented people. We are proud to be a Certified Great Place to Work®, recognized for a culture that prioritizes both professional excellence and employee well-being. In addition to a great work environment, we provide a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, and generous paid time off. Our offerings also include tuition and training assistance, BrightHorizons lifestyle assistance, life and disability insurance, and wellness programs. For more information on what it's like to work with us, please visit Life at Kastle.

Responsibilities

Strategic Pursuit Leadership

Serve as the overall pre-sales team leader for all Regional and National strategic account opportunities, coordinating the activities of sales engineers, solutions engineers, sub-contractors, and operations resources.
Partner with Strategic Account Managers to define client outcomes, establish win strategy, and shape the overall proposal approach.
Identify and define the full pre-sales resource requirements - people, skills, schedule, and budget needed to compete and win.
Lead client-facing outcome alignment sessions from initial qualification through go-live, ensuring client expectations are clearly defined and documented throughout.
Develop and maintain a detailed pre-sale project plan and pursuit strategy for each active strategic opportunity.

Proposal Development & Scope Ownership

Own the full proposal package for strategic pursuits: project scope of work, exclusions, preliminary project schedule (Gantt), sub-contractor RFQs and quotes, assumptions, and risk log.
Review sales engineering BOMs for completeness, dependencies, and unique site requirements; flag gaps prior to proposal submission.
Draft scope of work exclusions to protect Kastle from post-contract scope creep and change orders.
Ensure all proposal deliverables — drawings, BOMs, assumptions, pricing, and project schedule — are accurate, complete, and aligned with client requirements.
Lead large project reviews with sales and operations leadership on strategic opportunities to confirm scope, pricing model, and approval timeline.
Develop and deliver client presentation strategy for strategic pursuits; present with the account team when required.

Contract-to-Kickoff Transition

Own the contract-to-kickoff handoff- establishing the project channel, populating the project SharePoint folder (BOM, drawings, photos, sub quotes, outcome notes), and conducting a formal kickoff with the regional PM and Sales.
Develop the post-sale PM transition plan and ensure all project management continuity documentation is complete before transferring accountability to operations.
Identify post-sale project management involvement requirements and escalation protocols at proposal stage.

Post-Sale Oversight & Escalation

Co-own the Gantt chart with the regional PM during installation; update weekly and flag schedule risks to the National Account Manager before they reach the client.
Coordinate cross-functional dependencies — elevator vendors, GC schedules, turnstile sub-contractors, tenant provisioning, Kastle operations — to keep strategic projects on track.
Serve as the escalation point when operations encounters design ambiguity or scope questions during installation.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Serve as the connective layer between sales, sales engineering, solutions engineering, integrations, operations, and strategic sub-contractors throughout the pre-sales lifecycle.
Provide feedback to product and engineering teams on client needs, field integration challenges, and recurring proposal gaps.
Support development of client-specific marketing materials and executive-level presentations in partnership with the National Account Manager.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, project management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
7–10+ years of experience in project management, program management, or business development — with demonstrated success managing complex, multi-stakeholder pursuits or deployments.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive accountability without direct management authority.
Experience managing technically complex projects in the field — particularly systems integration, security, AV, construction, or similar — is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with physical security platforms (access control, CCTV, visitor management) is a plus; deep technical design expertise is not required.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to ownership groups, developers, and executive-level clients.
Strong command of project scheduling tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent).
Analytical and problem-solving mindset with strong attention to scope and risk.
PMP certification is a plus, but not required
This position requires approximately 25–30% travel across Kastle regions.

At Kastle, we believe that diversity makes us stronger - at work and in the world. Kastle Systems International, LLC is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or any other basis protected by applicable federal or state laws.

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $125,000-$140,000 annually, depending on experience, skills, education, and other job-related factors. This range reflects base pay only and may not include bonus, commission, equity, or other incentive compensation, where applicable. Actual offers are determined individually based on the candidate's qualifications and internal equity considerations. Kastle Systems (and its affiliate, i2G) offers a competitive benefits package, which may include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, and other benefits, depending on the position and location.

Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?

At Leica Microsystems, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.

You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

Shape the Future with Us!

At Leica Microsystems, we have been shaping the future for over 175 years with groundbreaking optical and digital solutions. With a culture rooted in customer focus, innovation, and teamwork, we lead the market in microscopy, imaging, and analysis, unveiling the invisible and empowering our customers to build a better, healthier world.

Joining Leica Microsystems means contributing to scientific discoveries and supporting surgeons in making critical decisions. The Commercial Training & Competency Program Manager is responsible for designing, deploying, and governing a global and consistent commercial capability development framework across all Regions. This role partners closely with Regional Commercial Leaders, Business Units (BUs), and DBS leaders to build a robust and scalable learning ecosystem, strengthen sales competencies, and ensure commercial teams perform at their highest potential.

This role requires an experienced commercial leader with strong understanding of sales cycles and process in a B2B environment, customer engagement, and commercial excellence practices. The role is both strategic and hands-on, driving global alignment while enabling local execution.

This position reports to the Director Global Commercial Operations and will be part of the Global Commercial Operations team.

The position will be fully remote in Italy.

In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To

Develop and lead the global commercial training strategy by establishing a consistent, scalable learning framework, onboarding programs, and blended learning solutions across all regions.
Build and govern a global sales competency framework that defines required capabilities, assesses proficiency, identifies gaps, and drives development plans for all commercial roles.
Partner with Regional Commercial Leaders, Business Units, and DBS teams to align training priorities, ensure content relevance, and drive accountability for capability development.
Establish robust training governance and operational excellence through standardized processes, content management, reporting, compliance oversight, learning platforms, and Train-the-Trainer networks.
Measure impact and continuously improve commercial capabilities by tracking training effectiveness, monitoring competency progress, analyzing performance gaps, and providing actionable insights to leadership.

The Essential Requirements Of The Job Include

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Business, Training & Development, Commercial Management, or comparable experience
7+ years in Sales, Commercial Excellence, Sales Enablement, or Training roles
Demonstrated ability to build and manage global programs and projects
Excellent facilitation, communication, and influencing skills
Strong command of MS Office, and in particular MS Excel and large language model (LLM) based answer engines such as M365 Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude

Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements

Ability to travel 20% of time

It would be a plus if you also possess experience in:

Working knowledge with Learning Management Systems (Cornerstone, Workday Learning)

jobs.title: Strategic Business Manager/Strategic Program Manager
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Strategic Business Manager owns one or more Strategic or Global Accounts of client organizations with scaled state, national, or global facilities and carries a personal revenue/quota and performance target tied to the account(s) assigned. This role leads a dedicated account team through the full account lifecycle: presale and solution development, design, contracting, and handoff for installation and maintenance, then stays accountable for the account's ongoing health and growth.

The account team led by the Strategic Business Program Manager fully represents the customer inside the company. The team develops the account, owns the sales process end to end, and is accountable for the quality and success of everything delivered against it, executing installation and service through the account's engineering and technical staff. The Strategic Business Manager does not simply oversee a sale; they own the customer's outcome from first contact through ongoing delivery. They manage a Team designed to represent the customer through sales, project management, admin and billing, and technical subject matter expertise tailored for the customer.

Scope scales with account size and complexity: a single large, complex account may require the Strategic Business Manager's full attention leading one team, while several smaller or less complex accounts may be grouped under one Strategic Business Manager leading multiple account teams. In either case, this role is the client's primary point of contact and the first line of leadership for their account team, reporting directly to the VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.

Organizational Structure & Team

Each account team led by the Strategic Business Manager is the customer's full representation inside the company — owning process, quality, and delivery outcomes, not just the initial sale. The team includes:

Account Executive or Account Manager: AE for developing accounts still building toward maturity; AM for mature, established accounts. Owns day-to-day sales motion and client relationship under this role's direction.
Administrator: Supports account operations, documentation, client-facing coordination, billing functions, scheduling, and coordination.
Project Manager or Project Coordinator: Owns project planning and execution once a sale moves into design and contracting. Handles presale and post sale due to multiple stakeholders and potentially long sales cycles. PM/PC is also ensuring communication and deliverables are customized and dedicated specifically for the customer.
Systems Technician: Coordinates with internal and external engineering and technical staff and the dedicated technical delivery team to execute installation and service, and is accountable for the quality of that delivery. The Systems Technician will be an SME (Subject Matter Expert) to ensure success, customer needs are communicated and met, and forecast planning and needs on behalf of the customer.

Roles & Responsibilities

Account Ownership & Customer Representation

Fully represent the customer inside and outside the company: own the account's process, quality, and delivery outcomes from first contact through ongoing service, not just the initial sale.
Carry a personal revenue/quota and performance target across assigned account(s); own forecasting and pipeline accuracy for those accounts.
Own the client relationship at multiple levels for assigned accounts, ensuring the account's strategy aligns with client objectives and company capacity.
Identify and pursue expansion, renewal, and cross-sell opportunities within existing accounts.
Work with leadership and vendor peers for solutions and strategies.

Sales Process & Delivery Oversight

Own the sales process for assigned accounts from opportunity through contracting, including proposal development and pricing decisions within approved authority.
Oversee handoff from contracting into design, installation, and maintenance, ensuring the account team and the account's engineering and technical staff are aligned on scope, schedule, and quality.
Own the quality of everything delivered against the account, working through the Systems Technician and engineering/technical staff to execute installation and service to standard.
Monitor project and service delivery performance against SLA and client expectations for assigned accounts.

Team Leadership

Directly manage the Account Executive/Account Manager, Administrator, Project Manager/Coordinator, and Systems Technician assigned to each account team.
Set individual and team performance expectations; coach, develop, and provide day-to-day direction.
Recommend hiring, staffing, and structure changes for account teams as accounts grow or shift in complexity.

Escalation & Cross-Functional Coordination

Serve as first point of escalation for client, delivery, or internal issues within assigned accounts; resolve directly or engage the appropriate internal team.
Escalate issues beyond this role's authority, cross-departmental blockers, resourcing conflicts, or client-relationship risk to the Director or VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.
Coordinate with other Strategic Business Managers and the dedicated technical delivery team to maintain consistent quality and process across the division.

Reporting

Provide regular account health, adopted portfolio, total solution targets, pipeline, and delivery status reporting to the Director or VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.
Maintain accurate account and opportunity data in CRM/ERP systems used by the division.
P&L Responsibilities
Utilization, AHR (Avg Hourly Rates), Margin, and other assigned leading or lagging indicators

Education And/or Experience

5+ years in strategic/enterprise account management or sales leadership, with a track record of carrying and meeting quota.
Experience managing multi-site or multi-facility client relationships (20+ locations preferred) from sale through delivery.
Experience directly managing a multi-disciplinary team (sales, project management, technical/field coordination roles).
Experience in systems integration, security, telecommunications, or a related technical products/services industry preferred.
Comfortable owning escalations and coordinating across departments to resolve client-impacting issues.
Familiarity with CRM/ERP and project/service management systems.
Willingness to travel to client sites as required by assigned accounts.

Company Overview

Day Wireless Systems is the largest full-service wireless integrator in the West. We provide design, construction, licensing, sales, service, rentals, installation, and maintenance for a wide range of wireless voice, data, and video applications.

Founded in 1969, today we have 30 locations and 400+ employees in California, Oregon, Washington, Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Day Wireless employees enjoy the opportunity to grow and transfer within our many locations and business divisions.

jobs.description:

Moses Lake Industries, Inc. (MLI) is a rapidly growing producer of ultra-pure chemical products, serving the semiconductor and flat-panel screen industries worldwide. We deliver world class products to the leaders of the industries we serve.

You will be working for a midsized company with great people and a history of steady growth and profitability. Sound like a match? If you are prepared to work in an exciting and rewarding environment, we look forward to considering your experience and qualifications.

Shift/Hours/Location:
M-F, 8am-5pm, Onsite/Hybrid, Moses Lake, WA

What You Will Be Working On

End-to-End Product Oversight: Manage and coordinate all aspects of multiple technical products, including product development, market analysis, supply chain optimization, cost structure evaluation, and profitability assessment.
Product Vision & Strategy: Define product vision, strategy, and roadmap. Gather, manage, and prioritize market and customer requirements while providing guidance and support to the program management team.

Customer-Centric Innovation: Define customer requirements for next-generation products to drive innovation and competitiveness.
Phase Gate Reviews: Lead and approve all tasks and deliverables for Phase 0 and Phase 1, and review/approve subsequent Phase Gate Reviews (PGR).
Business Case Development: Develop and realize comprehensive business cases to support product initiatives and strategic investments.
Costing Oversight: Approve costing/proposed pricing and assist with complex requests, including new warehousing solutions and shipping challenges.
Forecast Validation: Run and validate forecasting models to ensure accuracy and alignment with business objectives.
Customer Requirements Review: Assess new customer requirements, coordinate with internal teams, and identify process improvements or gaps necessary to meet customer expectations.
Strategic Alignment: Drive product and customer strategy, ensuring clear communication and alignment across internal stakeholder groups while troubleshooting issues.
Escalation Management: Handle Level 3 customer escalations and OCAP (Out-of-Control Action Plan) support, including preparation of escalation materials, participation in OCAP meetings as needed, and coordination with TM, PM, AM, QA, and QC teams for responses.
Cost Reduction Initiatives: Develop and implement cost reduction strategies to optimize profitability.
Continuous Improvement: Lead planning and execution of continuous improvement initiatives across processes and operations.
Audit Participation: Support major customer audits and provide ongoing assistance for corrective action responses.
Collaborating with Senior Planning Manager in costing and pricing for new products and/or customers (including location), including review with AM, support for PM/PLM
FSC for new product lines/packaging changes for owned RFQs
Initiate and/or Drive MOCs related to plant-wide changes, major expansions, or customer-sensitive changes (bulk sulfuric, building expansion, etc.).
Provide customer requirements for all MOCs. Final approver on closure of MOCs.
Costing & Pricing Management: Collaborate with Senior Planning Manager in costing and pricing for new products and/or customers, including location-specific considerations. Collaborate with Account Managers (AM) and provide support to Program Managers (PM) and Product Lifecycle Managers (PLM).
Financial Structure Control (FSC): Collaborate with Senior Planning Manager in FSC activities for new product lines and packaging changes related to owned RFQs.
Management of Change (MOC): Initiate and/or lead MOCs for plant-wide changes, major expansions, or customer-sensitive modifications (e.g., bulk sulfuric handling, building expansions). Define customer requirements for all MOCs and serve as the final approver for MOC closures.
Product Change Notification (PCN): Prepare PCN notifications for assigned MOCs, including data presentation, SPC documentation, generic and customer-specific notification forms, and additional requirements such as CoA comparison tables and MERF compliance.
Uphold all MLI policies and “MLI Code of Conduct.”
Strict compliance with Environmental and Safety regulations.
Compliance and individual accountability with the MLI Quality System and ISO Registration is required. It is the employee’s commitment to ensure that the Company’s actual practices and procedures are exercised as directed.
Perform other duties as assigned to support and sustain a high-performing team.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, Business Administration, or a related technical field. Or minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in related field, ideally in semiconductor chemicals, specialty chemicals, or advanced materials manufacturing.
Experience with New Product Development (NPD) processes and stage-gate methodologies.
Experience developing and presenting business cases to senior leadership for strategic investment decisions.
Semiconductor industry knowledge: Understanding of semiconductor-grade chemical specifications, metrology standards, and customer quality expectations (e.g., CoA, SPC, MERF compliance).
Management of Change (MOC) process expertise, particularly for plant-wide or customer-sensitive changes.
Product Change Notification (PCN) preparation and management.
Supply chain fundamentals: Understanding of warehousing, logistics, packaging, and shipping challenges relevant to chemical products.
Financial acumen: Strong understanding of costing, pricing, FSC (Financial Structure Control), and RFQ processes.
Strategic planning & road mapping: Ability to define product vision, strategy, and roadmaps.
Data-driven decision making: Ability to leverage KPIs and dashboards for performance management.
Cross-functional leadership: Ability to coordinate across various technical teams.
Escalation management: Composure and skill in handling customer escalations and OCAP processes.
Stakeholder communication: Clear, strategic communication to ensure alignment across internal groups.
Advisory & mentoring capability: Serving as an advisor to the program team on tasks and operations.
Audit readiness: Experience supporting major customer audits and driving corrective action responses.
Professionalism: Consistent demonstration of professionalism in appearance, conduct, and attitude.
Working knowledge of computers and MS Office software.
Working knowledge of arithmetic and grammar.
Demonstrated ability to:
Follow written and verbal instructions in English.
Manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously to meet established deadlines.
Work as a team and/or independently.
Perform tasks with attention to detail and accuracy.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.

Preferred Qualifications

Masters/MBA degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, Business Administration, or a related technical field.
PMP (Project Management Professional) or similar program/project management certification preferred.
Six Sigma / Lean certification (Green Belt or higher).
Experience in high-purity chemical manufacturing environments.
Demonstrated experience managing full product lifecycles — from concept through Phase Gate Reviews (PGR) to market launch and sustaining.
Proven track record in P&L management, including cost structure analysis, pricing strategy, and profitability optimization.
Financial acumen: Strong understanding of costing, pricing, FSC (Financial Structure Control), and RFQ processes.
Market research & analysis: Ability to conduct global supply-demand analysis, capacity assessments, and pricing trend evaluations.
Forecasting: Experience running and validating forecasting models.
Familiarity with semiconductor customer audit requirements (e.g., IATF, ISO standards relevant to the industry).
Experience with CRM tools for customer strategy management.
Comfort with AI-assisted tools and digital transformation initiatives.

Salary & Benefits

Please note that the salary information shown below is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate experience and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

Summary pay range: $85K-$125K

Located in central Washington, an outdoor recreational oasis, we offer the following benefits: compensation, medical, vision, and dental insurance benefits.

Generous PTO: Your off time is important.
Medical/Dental/Vision: Majority of premiums paid by MLI. Includes virtual medical and mental health options.
Additional Health Coverage: FSA and HSA available. Voluntary insurance options include life and AD&D, accident, hospitalization, and critical illness.
Earn More: We offer a generous discretionary bonus program in addition to salary/wage.
401(k) Savings Plan: Jump start your retirement with MLI’s employer matching contributions.
Company-Paid Benefits: Long-Term Disability Insurance, EAP, Fitness Club Membership Program, & Education Assistance Program. Relocation Assistance available.
Additional Benefits: We provide position-based clothing, travel expenses, training and additional materials needed on a case-by-case basis.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Duties are generally performed indoors in an office and high purity manufacturing environment. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderate. When working in the presence of safety hazards, the employee is expected to follow company safety rules and use proper personal protective equipment such as: hardhat, safety glasses and full leather shoes, etc. Employees will work in a covered Process Safety Management (PSM) environment containing threshold quantities of flammable liquids and/or gasses that have a potential for fire or explosion. Employees working in this environment are required to be free from devices that are not considered intrinsically safe. Examples of devices that may not be intrinsically safe include Insulin Pumps, Pacemakers, Pain Management devices, etc.

This Assistant Director role is designed for a project leader who can connect strategy to execution, bring together cross-functional teams, and drive outcomes that reduce enterprise risk while supporting business value and operational resilience.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead complex global information security programs and projects from initiation through delivery, ensuring scope, plans, milestones, risks, budgets and outcomes are actively managed.
Translate enterprise security objectives into clear execution plans that support business value, measurable benefits and risk reduction.
Coordinate cross-functional and geographically distributed teams across Information Security, Enterprise Technology, Client Technology, Member Firms, vendors and contractors.
Drive project governance, status reporting, issue escalation and decision-making with senior stakeholders and executive sponsors.
Develop and manage detailed project plans, timelines, dependencies and RAID items using project management platforms and tools such as MS Project, Azure DevOps or equivalent tools.
Identify risks, issues, interdependencies and resource constraints across programs, busy seasons and organizational priorities, and develop pragmatic mitigation plans.
Facilitate stakeholder alignment by integrating feedback, resolving conflicts and keeping teams focused on shared outcomes.
Support continuous improvement of security processes, governance practices and delivery methods, including lessons learned and sustainable operating models.
Mentor and coach project team members, build team engagement, and encourage accountability, collaboration and quality delivery.

Technical and security knowledge: Understanding of information security technologies, including cloud, network, perimeter, messaging, endpoint and data security, along with familiarity with security frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001 and CIS Controls.
Project management depth: Proven ability to manage complex information security projects, including iterative and waterfall delivery methods, planning, budget management, risk management and stakeholder governance.
Leadership without authority: Ability to build trusted relationships, motivate teams, establish a shared vision and drive delivery across teams that do not directly report to the role.
Executive communication: Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to simplify technical matters for non-technical stakeholders and present concise, data-driven updates to senior leadership.
Stakeholder engagement: Ability to engage executive leadership and key stakeholders, understand competing priorities and negotiate alignment at multiple levels of the organization.
Risk and issue management: Ability to anticipate delivery risks, assess business impact, make timely recommendations and drive mitigation through structured plans.
Problem solving: Strong analytical thinking, critical judgment, creativity and conflict-resolution skills in time-sensitive or ambiguous situations.
Global mindset: Comfort operating across cultures, geographies, Member Firms and organizational structures, including awareness of political, regulatory and commercial factors that may affect delivery.

To qualify for the role you must have

Proven experience leading complex global information security, technology or risk-related programs from initiation to closure.

jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
Experience with statistical analytics and programming languages such as R, Python, Ruby, etc.

jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
