jobs.description:
Alice's RL Gyms team builds adversarial environments and evaluations that the world's leading AI labs use to test and train their most capable agents. Every engagement is a delivery project: a lab specifies what it needs to measure, and we produce the environments, adversarial tasks, and verifiers that measure it, against a deadline and a quality bar the customer sets.

Our customers are the frontier labs. You'll work alongside the people building the models everyone else is reading about, on the problems they haven't solved yet, and what you ship becomes part of how they decide whether an agent is safe to release. Very few roles put you that close to the frontier.

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own those projects. You'll run several lab engagements at once, each with its own researchers, engineers, and reviewers. You decide who works on what, you hold the schedule, and you decide whether a batch is good enough to ship.
The field is cutting-edge, and the projects change shape faster than any playbook can describe.

What you'll do

Project ownership

Own concurrent lab engagements end-to-end: scope, milestones, delivery, and status
Turn a customer specification into a task plan with your researchers and engineers: how many tasks, in which environments, against which models, by when
Track every batch through the pipeline (in progress, under review, approved, delivered) and keep the delivery record accurate enough that anyone can read the state of a project in a minute
Surface a slipping deadline early, with the tradeoff already worked out: cut scope, add capacity, or move the date

Researcher allocation and quality

Allocate researchers, task writers, and reviewers across projects based on throughput and specialty
Own their onboarding: brief them on the environment, the attack pattern, and the acceptance criteria, then get them to their first accepted task fast
Give quality feedback on rejected work and spot the patterns behind repeat rejections
Manage the review chain so that no batch reaches the customer before it has cleared internal review

What we're looking for

2 to 4 years in project management, program management, or product management, in a role where you owned a delivery and not just a workstream
High autonomy in an undefined space. The right answer to “what's the process for this?” is usually that you write it
Comfortable managing contributors you don't line-manage: setting expectations, giving direct feedback, and making the call when quality doesn't come up
Fluent written and spoken English

Advantage

A technical background: industrial engineering, computer science, information systems, or equivalent hands-on experience
Exposure to LLMs or AI agents, whether professional or self-taught
Background in security, red teaming, or trust and safety
Experience coordinating a distributed or contract contributor team
Data fluency: SQL, spreadsheets, or scripting well enough to answer your own questions about project throughput

Alice is a trust, safety, and security company built for the AI era. We safeguard the communicative technologies people use to create, collaborate, and interact- whether with each other or with machines.

In a world where AI has fundamentally changed the nature of risk, Alice provides end-to-end coverage across the entire AI lifecycle. We support frontier model labs, enterprises, and UGC platforms with a comprehensive suite of solutions: from model hardening evaluations and pre-deployment red-teaming to runtime guardrails and ongoing drift detection.

Alice is widely considered a global leader in online safety and AI security. We have some of the most forward-thinking and passionate minds in the world working to safeguard over 3 billion users across the largest AI and tech platforms.

If you're creative and driven to secure the future of AI, we want to hear from you!

Description

This Sr. Program Manager role will lead a program within Financial Integrity Trust (FIT), a team embedded within the Financial Risk Mitigation (FRM) organization. FIT is focused on financial integrity of engagement between seller and Amazon by ensuring a secure, transparent, and trustworthy financial relationship between Amazon and its sellers. It is a critical line of defense, stopping bad actors from profiting while ensuring a frictionless experience for SPs. We track “who” is profiting and “where” Amazon disburses funds, and own “when” disbursements occur. We ensure appropriate controls, verifications, and validations for both charge and disbursement instruments, reducing bad actors’ ability to scale fraud and ensure compliance. We also compute and withhold account-level disbursement reserves, govern payment speed, and recover funds from enforced sellers, preventing unpaid fees and misuse of funds.

Mitigate financial risk and stop bad actors from profiting by building tools and setting policies that control how quickly sellers are paid and disburse. This role will work closely with product, tech, policy, legal, and finance stakeholders and partner teams.

Organization Summary:

If you love the pursuit of excellence and are inspired by the challenges that come through driving innovations that impact how the world lives, works, and plays, then we invite you to learn more about Microsoft Operations - and the value we deliver across Microsoft, our partners, and our customers. We make doing business with Microsoft easy.

Microsoft Enterprise Direct Operations, within Microsoft Business Operations, provides direct and centralized operations services for Strategic Direct customers to transact with Microsoft. We are accountable to design and executing transactional services across the customer’s licensing lifecycle. We relentlessly pursue process efficiency, timeliness, quality, and compliance, all while providing world class Customer experience. We are looking for team members to join our team focused on delivering Customer experience with deep expertise in Microsoft Licensing and Quote to Cash Processes.

We are looking for a Process Program Manager to join our team and drive the planning, execution, and optimization of our strategic programs. You will be responsible for overseeing the program lifecycle, from design to execution, ensuring that the program objectives, scope, schedule, quality, and benefits are aligned with the organizational goals and stakeholder expectations. You will also be responsible for driving continuous improvement and change management across the program, identifying and resolving issues, risks, and dependencies, and ensuring effective communication and collaboration among the program team and stakeholders.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities

Process Management

Accountable for end-to-end process performance by executing compliant processes and controls, anticipating and logging risk, and documenting process flows, systems, and requirements. Provides data, research, and assessment results to enable an enterprise view of the process and inform decision-making.
Monitors metrics and KPIs, performs analysis and benchmarking, and identifies opportunities to improve efficiency, customer experience, and cost. Facilitates stakeholder collaboration and change management efforts, applying process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma), AI and compiling business cases and feedback to drive continuous optimization.

Business Program Planning and Design

Performs program landscape research and analysis, forecasting, and examines business trends (e.g., customer feedback and expectations) to identify audience size and program scope, and stay current and agile.
Understands overall business goals, objectives, and strategies, as well as short- and long-term business priorities.
Understands and identifies current program risks, impact, and mitigation plans.
Identifies and scopes opportunities to improve current programs. Identifies and provides solutions to root problems, defines the program strategy, gathers program requirements, identifies resource needs, creates the project plan and targets, and works across teams to align on the plan of record. Drives clarity in complex program issues and strives for simplification.
Works with cross-functional stakeholders to design compliant, complex programs from initiation to delivery with minimal coaching. Produces collateral (e.g., proposals, strategy walking deck, internal and external pitch content) to incorporate stakeholder needs and ensure the business objectives are met.
Defines and tracks the success criteria and performance metrics and Key Performance Indicators [KPIs], such as quality, adoption, usage, impact, and effectiveness for the program.

Business Program Management

Contributes to or leads a portfolio of projects including the project plan, timelines, milestones, financial management, performance metrics, and/or resource needs for complex programs. Communicates the program status and risk to relevant stakeholders and holds them accountable for following the established schedule, risk mitigation plans, and processes.

Business Program Excellence and Execution

Defines and executes on landing change management plans. Leads the rhythm of business (ROB) during plan execution to ensure participants and stakeholders are communicating and responding according to the necessary cadence. Works across teams to ensure all program requirements are understood and can be met.
Enables execution teams as program subject matter experts to resolve complex Customer scenarios.

Business Program Evaluation and Improvement

Conducts cost-benefit analyses to examine performance to value drivers. Contributes to monthly business review (MBR) and runs rhythms regularly to identify what is working and what is not, and makes improvements accordingly.
Collects and evaluates success criteria and performance metrics, Key Performance Indicators [KPIs], and customer feedback, and uses scorecards and dashboards to monitor complex programs and ensure all activities align with business and program objectives. Uses data analytics to derive insights and training that help identify current and future program risks and mitigation plans, as well as opportunities to streamline and optimize programs based on lessons learned.
Utilizes direction and strategy from leadership regarding business area of expertise in order to help create and execute plans that shift current priorities to new organizational initiatives and objectives, and influences others to change behavior accordingly. Defines vision and strategy for change, broad and specific impact, and the flow of communication to the organization. Ensures buy in and adoption of the new program or change by others in the organization. Develops the collateral required to enable key stakeholders and others to be on board. Contributes to the training, reskilling, and mapping of individuals in partnership with Human Resources (HR).

Amazon's Last Mile In-Life Services team is looking for a Senior Program Manager, Retrofit Strategy & Execution to own the end-to-end operational execution of large-scale vehicle retrofit campaigns across North America. This role is the hands-on execution engine for retrofit programs ranging from $10M–$50M, turning approved plans into completed installations across hundreds of delivery stations with zero disruption to daily delivery operations. It will also own strategic projects to improve customer experience on both Retrofits and Tires.

You will manage the full installation lifecycle — from VIN identification and parts logistics through on-site night-shift installations, vendor coordination, completion reporting, invoice validation, and campaign closeout. You will work across fleet systems, coordinate with Delivery Service Partners (DSPs), Regional Fleet Managers (RFMs), and multiple installation vendors to keep campaigns on schedule, on budget, and at quality. This is an operationally intensive role that requires comfort with ambiguity, strong vendor management instincts, and the ability to drive execution at scale in a fast-moving logistics environment.

Travel: Up to 25% (delivery station site visits, vendor oversight, pilot installations)

Own the live installation schedule across vendors, delivery stations, and regions — adjusting in real time for VIN availability, vendor capacity, and site constraints while ensuring zero disruption to daytime delivery operations
Manage daily VIN tracking and reconciliation across branded fleet and Last Mile Rental systems; own parts receiving, site storage, and vehicle availability at delivery stations
Coordinate multi-vendor installation operations including scheduling, on-site field oversight, completion reporting, and go-back/rework resolution
Validate vendor invoices against confirmed completion data; track labor and material costs against $10M–$50M campaign budgets
Manage daily DS/DSP communication across multiple channels to confirm vehicle availability and resolve scheduling conflicts
Build network rollout plans — quantities, locations, and sequencing — and own PO submissions, workback plans, and procurement alignment
Drive campaign closeout including inventory reconciliation, maintenance and repair handoff, warranty documentation, and lessons learned
Provide weekly dashboard updates on completion status, cost performance, and quality metrics to leadership

A day in the life

This role will interact with DSPs, RFMs, product owners, and vendors nearly daily to ensure success, control cost and quality.

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Your greatest work is ahead!

The Intelligence Sector seeks a highly qualified and trained Journeyman-level Cyberspace Intelligence Threat Analysts to support United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM) operations, with focus on identifying, analyzing, and recommending mitigation strategies for Cyber threats targeting Offensive Cyberspace Operations (OCO) systems. This vital on-site support to USCYBERCOM J3 (Operations), Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and Joint Task Force-Ares (JTF-ARES) underpins USCYBERCOM support to United States National Security objectives.

What You’ll Be Doing

Provide timely, accurate, relevant support in manner that best supports USCYBERCOM in identifying and assessing emerging threats and vulnerabilities in the Cyberspace domain, with focus on risks to OCO systems.
Analyze and evaluate All-Source finished intelligence, single-source intelligence, and technical data from various sources to identify Cyber threat patterns and anomalies.
Produce and deliver recurring threat intelligence reports, summarizing relevant cyber threats to OCO infrastructure.
Conduct and publish in-depth risk assessments to evaluate and categorize the risk posture of detected cyber threats while supporting development and refinement of risk assessment methodologies and tools used for threat categorization.
Utilize Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) tools and apply analytical methodologies when required to perform technical analysis on critical Cyber threats impacting OCO assets.
Collaborate with operational, technical, and intelligence elements across USCYBERCOM to enhance situational awareness and threat response capabilities.
Maintain a current understanding of advanced persistent threats (APTs), threat actor tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), and cyber threat trends affecting national security.
Maintain situational awareness of, and execute on demand, Cyberspace Operations (CO) crisis plans.
Provide situational awareness to a range of projects, Crisis Action Teams, and current operations activities supporting Operational Planning Teams (OPTs).
Execute resource allocation decisions aligned with organization objectives.
Apply knowledge of cyber threats and attack methods and techniques emanating from state and non-state adversaries and tiered vulnerabilities within Blue Space as focus of threats.
Develop and execute comprehensive programs for assessing CO and validating operational performance characteristics.
Review, approve, prioritize, and submit operational requirements for research, development, and/or acquisition of cyber capabilities.
Support integration and synchronization of intelligence planning activities with operational planning timelines.
Interpret and apply laws, regulations, policies, and guidance relevant to daily activities.
Communicate complex information, concepts, or ideas in a confident and well-organized manner through verbal, written, and/or visual means.

Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility and Polygraph required.
BA/BS degree or higher within Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Intelligence Studies, or related field, or ability to complete degree within one year of hire. Can substitute formal education with extended experience and technical certifications.
Five plus years’ experience within Cyber intelligence analysis or a similar Cyber threat analyst role, or eight plus years’ total within field of intelligence analysis.
Demonstrated understanding of All-Source intelligence principles as applied to field of Cyber.
Demonstrated experience with applicable SIGINT tools and techniques and able to produce single-source intelligence products tailored to drive CO.
Broad knowledge of Blue-space Cyber capabilities and demonstrate understanding of available Cyber infrastructure or platforms to conduct Defensive (DCO) and Offensive Cyberspace Operations (OCO).
Knowledge of the range of CO and their underlying intelligence support needs, topics, and focus areas.
Knowledge of computer networking fundamentals as well as concepts, terminology, and operations of a wide range of communications media (computer and telephone networks, satellite, fiber, wireless).
Ability to support timely, accurate, relevant analytical production, to include documents, summaries, issue papers, talking points, and briefings
Demonstrated proficiency working in a fast-paced collaborative environment, ability to proactively multi-task and meet short deadlines.
Strong interpersonal, critical thinking, and communication skills, including the ability to clearly convey complex and technical data to non-technical consumers.

Favorable If You Have

Masters’ Degree or higher within Cybersecurity, Intelligence Studies, Information Security or related fields.
Intimate familiarity with USCYBERCOM organizational structure and mission.
Prior experience supporting Joint operations across multiple warfighting domains.
Demonstrated experience incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into operations at any level to increase efficiency and effectiveness of operational outcomes
Experience with Space-enabled CO.
Formal training within field of Cyber Warfare and Joint Operations.
Familiar with art of Data Science and applicability to CO.
Familiar with Microsoft Power BI data visualization software.
Familiarity with Cyber threat frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK or Cyber Kill Chain.
Desired Certifications: DoD 8570 IAT Level II (CCNA Security, COMPTIA CySA+, COMPTIA Security + CE, GICSP, GSEC, SSCP).

Amentum is seeking a driven and professional Epidemiology Operations Senior Analyst
to work on the PACOM Command Surgeon’s (J07) Decision Support Team (DST). This position serves as the DST's senior expert for infectious-disease surveillance, population-health trends, and epidemiological risk, acting as a primary liaison with civilian health agencies, academia, and foreign partners. The Analyst leads wastewater-based epidemiology and integrates public health, biosurveillance, wastewater, open-source, operational, and classified information to identify anomalies and assess force-health and mission effects. General public health experience without applied epidemiological or biosurveillance expertise is insufficient. Assigned to J85, the position directly supports J07, entails hybrid work from Camp Smith and other local locations, receives functional priorities from J07 through established contract channels, operates with project and technical oversight from J85, and reports administratively to the Amentum Project Lead.

Essential Responsibilities
:

Analyze epidemiological, public-health, wastewater, biosurveillance, operational, open-source, and classified information to identify trends, anomalies, clusters, and emerging threats.
Lead wastewater-surveillance baseline, indicator, trend, and anomaly-threshold development with laboratory, public-health, and CBRNE specialists.
Assess the significance, reliability, limitations, uncertainty, and operational implications of epidemiological findings.
Provide findings to the Operations Planner for integration with medical intelligence, CBRNE analysis, Force Health Protection, and operational plans.
Monitor emerging infectious diseases and public-health threats across the US PACOM AOR using DoW, interagency, state, foreign-government, and partner data.
Support epidemiological investigations and assessments in coordination with authorized DoW medical and public-health personnel.
Coordinate with J07, subordinate commands, theater public-health organizations, overseas laboratories, intelligence analysts, military planners, and external partners.
Test the Biosurveillance Information Platform and provide epidemiology-specific findings for Military Utility Assessments and recommendations.
Translate surveillance needs into requirements for technical teams developing feeds, dashboards, alerts, and workflows; coding is not required.
Develop surveillance protocols, data-quality standards, analytic methods, reports, white papers, and capability-improvement recommendations.

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's degree or higher in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health science, or a closely related discipline.
Must have an active Secret security clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance.
7+ years of progressively responsible experience in epidemiology, public health surveillance, disease monitoring, outbreak analysis, or a related field.
Experience independently analyzing complex surveillance data and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Knowledge of epidemiological design, surveillance methods, statistical concepts, disease-activity measures, data quality, and uncertainty.
Familiarity with military planning and ability to work with military planners, intelligence professionals, technical teams, and decision-makers.
Strong writing, consultation, coordination, and senior-leader briefing skills.
Active Top-Secret security clearance, with SCI eligibility later during employment.
Master of Public Health or another relevant master's degree; wastewater-based epidemiology experience.
DoW, Combatant Command, public-health agency, or infectious-disease surveillance experience.
Knowledge of microbiology, pathophysiology, syndromic surveillance, and emerging diseases.
Indo-Pacific experience and familiarity with AI-enabled tools, Maven Smart System, or biosurveillance platforms.

jobs.title: Epidemiology Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Amentum is seeking a driven and professional Epidemiology Operations Senior Analyst
to work on the PACOM Command Surgeon’s (J07) Decision Support Team (DST). This position serves as the DST's senior expert for infectious-disease surveillance, population-health trends, and epidemiological risk, acting as a primary liaison with civilian health agencies, academia, and foreign partners. The Analyst leads wastewater-based epidemiology and integrates public health, biosurveillance, wastewater, open-source, operational, and classified information to identify anomalies and assess force-health and mission effects. General public health experience without applied epidemiological or biosurveillance expertise is insufficient. Assigned to J85, the position directly supports J07, entails hybrid work from Camp Smith and other local locations, receives functional priorities from J07 through established contract channels, operates with project and technical oversight from J85, and reports administratively to the Amentum Project Lead.

Essential Responsibilities
:

Analyze epidemiological, public-health, wastewater, biosurveillance, operational, open-source, and classified information to identify trends, anomalies, clusters, and emerging threats.
Lead wastewater-surveillance baseline, indicator, trend, and anomaly-threshold development with laboratory, public-health, and CBRNE specialists.
Assess the significance, reliability, limitations, uncertainty, and operational implications of epidemiological findings.
Provide findings to the Operations Planner for integration with medical intelligence, CBRNE analysis, Force Health Protection, and operational plans.
Monitor emerging infectious diseases and public-health threats across the US PACOM AOR using DoW, interagency, state, foreign-government, and partner data.
Support epidemiological investigations and assessments in coordination with authorized DoW medical and public-health personnel.
Coordinate with J07, subordinate commands, theater public-health organizations, overseas laboratories, intelligence analysts, military planners, and external partners.
Test the Biosurveillance Information Platform and provide epidemiology-specific findings for Military Utility Assessments and recommendations.
Translate surveillance needs into requirements for technical teams developing feeds, dashboards, alerts, and workflows; coding is not required.
Develop surveillance protocols, data-quality standards, analytic methods, reports, white papers, and capability-improvement recommendations.

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's degree or higher in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health science, or a closely related discipline.
Must have an active Secret security clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance.
7+ years of progressively responsible experience in epidemiology, public health surveillance, disease monitoring, outbreak analysis, or a related field.
Experience independently analyzing complex surveillance data and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Knowledge of epidemiological design, surveillance methods, statistical concepts, disease-activity measures, data quality, and uncertainty.
Familiarity with military planning and ability to work with military planners, intelligence professionals, technical teams, and decision-makers.
Strong writing, consultation, coordination, and senior-leader briefing skills.
Active Top-Secret security clearance, with SCI eligibility later during employment.
Master of Public Health or another relevant master's degree; wastewater-based epidemiology experience.
DoW, Combatant Command, public-health agency, or infectious-disease surveillance experience.
Knowledge of microbiology, pathophysiology, syndromic surveillance, and emerging diseases.
Indo-Pacific experience and familiarity with AI-enabled tools, Maven Smart System, or biosurveillance platforms.

Summary

This position is part of the Defense Human Resources Activity (Personnel Readiness Management Agency) . The incumbent Serves in a developmental training interdisciplinary position as a Statistician (Economics),Economist, or Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) assisting in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances and providing support with managing certain aspects of the BAH, OHA, Overseas COLA, and CONUS COLA programs.

Learn More About This Agency

Duties

Help

As a Interdisciplinary Statistician (Economics )/Economist/Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) At The GS-0110/1515/1530-7/9/11/12 Some Of Your Typical Work Assignments May Include

GS-7

Serves in a developmental capacity, assisting senior analysts in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances (BAH, OHA, COLA).
With close supervision, analyzes housing and cost-of-living data to help produce rate recommendations.
Assists in researching economic issues and reviewing data reports and statistical summaries to support rate suggestions.
Helps prepare reports, memorandums, and allowance materials for publication and dissemination.
Assists the team in responding to inquiries regarding allowance programs and survey results.

GS-9

Independently carries out recurring assignments to develop and analyze military housing and cost-of-living surveys.
Analyzes statistical and economic data to produce allowance rate recommendations in conformance with accepted policies.
Conducts in-depth reviews of data reports and statistical summaries, identifying and researching economic issues and facts for allowance determinations.
Prepares recommendations, reports, and responses to customer inquiries on allowance programs with limited supervisory review.
Designs and builds user-focused analytics to extract actionable information from diverse data sources to inform decision-makers.

GS-11

Plans and conducts a variety of complex studies on housing and cost-of-living programs, resolving difficult issues and interpreting policy.
Independently analyzes and defends rate-setting methodologies and makes recommendations that have a significant impact on service members.
Develops and refines analytical methods and procedures for data collection, validation, and the accomplishment of surveys.
Serves as a technical resource, providing professional assistance and advice to the Department on allowance programs.
Prepares and presents detailed briefings, complex analyses, and justifications for multiple audiences to defend findings and program recommendations.

GS-12

Serves as a senior analyst and subject matter expert responsible for the full lifecycle of developing, analyzing, and managing allowance programs.
Leads the most complex and critical analyses of economic and statistical data, formulating and defending final rate recommendations for senior leadership approval.
Presents and defends allowance programs and rate-setting methodologies against challenges and public scrutiny, representing the agency in high-level meetings.
Develops and implements new analytical techniques and criteria to improve program effectiveness and advises management on long-range plans and objectives.
Provides authoritative guidance and mentorship to junior analysts and coordinates with high-ranking officials across DoD, government agencies, and private sources.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

Must be a U.S. citizen
Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service
Resume and supporting documents (See How To Apply)
Suitable for Federal employment, determined by a background investigation
May be required to successfully complete a probationary period
Work Schedule: Full Time
Overtime: Occasionally
Tour of Duty: Flexible
Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized
Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA): Non-Exempt
Financial Disclosure: Not Required
Telework Eligibility: This position is telework eligible
This position may require occasional travel, as conditions allow.
This position is Noncritical-Sensitive, requiring a Secret clearance.

Qualifications

You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service:
Applying advanced statistical, economic, or operations-research principles to analyze and evaluate allowance-program issues and provide technical expertise on allowance programs.
Leading complex analytical projects involving the development or substantial revision of data-collection approaches, analytical techniques, or program-evaluation criteria.
Developing, presenting, and defending recommendations and analytical methodologies for complex allowance-program issues before senior officials, stakeholders, oversight bodies, or other public-facing audiences.

OR

Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree.

You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service:
Conducting comprehensive analyses of complex data using advanced statistical, economic, or data-science analytical and evaluative methods, and developing recommendations based on the results.
Modifying or adapting standard data-science and statistical techniques to address a range of analytical challenges, program issues, or policy questions.
Planning and carrying out complex studies, documenting and justifying findings, and presenting results to technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior officials.

OR

Master's or equivalent graduate degree.

You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service:
Applying established statistical, economic, or data-science methods to analyze and evaluate data for routine projects or assignments.
Independently using automated analytical tools, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar software, to extract, organize, and analyze information from complex data sources.
Resolving conventional problems in data collection and analysis by applying established program methodologies, procedures, and regulations.

OR

2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree.

OR

Possess some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and have more than one year of graduate level education as described, but less than two. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%.

You may qualify at the GS-07, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service:
Assisting with developmental assignments by applying statistical, economic, or data-science principles, methods, and techniques under guidance.
Using automated systems and software, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar tools, to access, retrieve, organize, and review data from multiple sources.
Assisting with research, interpretation, and evaluation of data using qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for well-precedented assignments.

OR

Possess: a Bachelor's degree w/Superior Academic Achievement or 1 year of graduate level education.

OR

Have some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and I have some but less than one year of graduate level education as described. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%.

In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0110/1515/1530 series.

If you are applying for the Economist0110 series, you must have the following.
Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus.
OR
Combination of education and experience courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education.
If you are applying for the Operations Research 1515 series, you must have the following.
Degree: in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics, Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science, optimization; mathematical modeling; queueing theory; engineering; physics (except descriptive or survey courses); econometrics; psychometrics; biometrics; experimental psychology; physical chemistry; industrial process analysis; managerial economics; computer science; measurement for management; mathematical models in social phenomena; and courses that involved application of operations research techniques and methodologies to problems of management, marketing, systems design, and other specialized fields; or other comparable quantitative analysis courses. OR
Combination of education and experience courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Implement risk management processes at the ground level for the construction finance business, gaining a thorough understanding of the project and developer and preparing a credit memo to assess the project viability and proposal structure as per ABHFL risk parameters and customer requirements. Key activities are analysis of project viability, assessment of market information and developer financials.

Job Context & Major Challenges

Job Context/ Job Challenges

Job Context

Key Aspects

The company has a well-defined vision of being one of the most reputed and material financiers within the lending space-spread across both retail HNI and corporate clientele. We have made significant investments in our process and system infrastructure towards preparing for the next level of growth and are one of the only financial entities certified for ISO 9001:2008 across all our business processes. Spread across 18 cities, we plan on further diversifying our risk and revenue mix through expansion into new geographies and new product segments allowing our customers a one-window shop for all their financing needs.

The Business Credit Analyst is an integral part of the Construction Finance Business and is responsible for analyzing the proposals with the required due diligence and to ensure that all information required to take a credit decision is captured in the proposal.

The analyst is also responsible to ensure that proposals are compliant with all the norms of credit policy, RBI regulations and other statutory regulations.

He/she has to maintain stipulated TAT in credit appraisal process and is also responsible for keeping update on the various changes in economic scenario, sectors, etc., co-ordination with sales team and RMG for faster decisions to improvise TATs of the overall sanction process.

Market Intelligence and understanding Competition best practices and suggesting changes in the existing product / policy and processes.

Generating various MISs and EWS (early warning signals), overall portfolio monitoring form risk as well as compliance perspective is an important job aspect.

Key Challenges

Cross functional coordination to enable timely approval of credit proposals

Self-updating on economic / sectoral changes in the economy

Improvising on TAT

Seamless co-ordination with multiple internal and external entities

New product development

Enabling Skill Sets & Qualifications

The critical skill sets are a strong analytical acumen, evaluation skills, detail orientation & decision-making skills, initiative & target orientation & market intelligence developed through a strong industry network.

The education & experience required to fulfil this profile are a Chartered Accountant or an MBA with minimum 2-4 years of experience in credit and risk functions of Banks/NBFCs.

jobs.title: Project Manager, European Industrial Partnerships | Chef de projet, Partenariats Européens industriels et Stratégiques
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure
using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite
, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California
, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast recherche un(e) Chef de projet – Partenariats industriels et Stratégiques
, rattaché(e) au Directeur des Politiques Publiques et des Relations Gouvernementales.

Le/la titulaire du poste aura pour mission d’identifier, de développer et de mettre en place des partenariats industriels européens, ainsi que d’assurer le pilotage de projets et de travaux de recherche liés aux activités de Vast en matière de vols spatiaux habités et de satellites en Europe. Il/elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes américaines de développement commercial.

L’un des principaux objectifs de ce poste sera de développer la dimension industrielle européenne de l’offre de Vast : identifier les fournisseurs et partenaires européens dont les capacités répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise, et structurer des partenariats soutenant les considérations de retour géographique et industriel associées aux opportunités institutionnelles, aux attributions de sièges et aux besoins d’approvisionnement plus larges de Vast, à court comme à long terme.

Vast Europe est une structure agile à taille humaine, et ce poste est volontairement polyvalent. Le/la titulaire contribuera aux travaux de recherche, au développement de partenariats, à la préparation de propositions, à l’organisation d’événements et à la coordination de projets, en appui aux deux directeurs.

Cette polyvalence constitue un élément central du poste. Si vous souhaitez participer concrètement au développement des vols spatiaux habités commerciaux, en collaboration avec les agences, les gouvernements et l’industrie, et que vous êtes à l’aise dans la gestion simultanée de plusieurs projets, ce poste est fait pour vous.

Il s’agit d’un poste à temps plein, en CDI, basé dans notre bureau de Paris, siège européen de Vast. Rémunération selon profil et expérience.

Principales responsabilités

Développer et maintenir une vision structurée de l’écosystème industriel européen pertinent pour Vast : fournisseurs, capacités, expertises nationales, pôles de compétences et partenaires potentiels dans les États membres.
Identifier, développer et contribuer à structurer des opportunités de partenariats industriels européens renforçant l’offre de Vast auprès des agences et clients gouvernementaux, notamment au travers d’arguments liés au retour géographique et industriel dans le cadre des campagnes d’attribution de sièges.
Mener des analyses approfondies du secteur spatial commercial européen, incluant les concurrents, programmes institutionnels, cycles de financement, évolutions réglementaires et dynamiques de marché, afin d’identifier les opportunités et les risques.
Préparer des notes de recherche ciblées, études de marché et documents de référence en amont des réunions clients, des propositions et des négociations.
Gérer la préparation des propositions, offres et réponses aux appels d’offres institutionnels, incluant la recherche, la rédaction et la coordination des contributions des équipes du siège de Vast et des partenaires européens.
Gérer les données CRM, les rapports de pipeline et les outils de suivi internes pour l’équipe européenne, et mettre en place des processus réguliers de reporting.
Piloter la planification et l’exécution de la présence de Vast lors de conférences européennes, journées sectorielles et événements clients.
Assurer la gestion de projets liés aux vols spatiaux habités et aux activités satellitaires, en appui aux deux directeurs et selon les priorités définies.
Assurer, selon les délégations reçues, l’intérim des directeurs sur les sujets liés aux partenariats industriels et à la recherche, et contribuer à l’intégration ainsi qu’au développement des membres juniors de l’équipe.

Profil du candidat

Professionnel(le) confirmé(e), curieux(se), rigoureux(se) et organisé(e), disposant d’une solide connaissance du secteur spatial européen, d’excellentes compétences en recherche et en rédaction, ainsi que d’une capacité avérée à conduire des analyses de manière autonome.
Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) est motivé(e) par un large éventail de responsabilités, sait gérer des projets de bout en bout avec un niveau limité de supervision, et s’épanouit dans un environnement agile, autonome et parfois imprévisible, propre à une petite structure européenne adossée à un siège américain dynamique.

Compétences et expérience requises

Diplôme de niveau licence ou supérieur en ingénierie, sciences, commerce, affaires internationales ou discipline connexe.
5 à 7 ans d’expérience minimum dans le secteur spatial, le développement commercial, les partenariats industriels, les achats, ou des fonctions liées à la recherche et à l’intelligence de marché.
Expérience directe avec des fournisseurs industriels européens, maîtres d’œuvre et/ou acteurs institutionnels.
Expérience avérée en tant qu’interface principale entre une entreprise ou un programme et un client externe, tant sur les aspects techniques que managériaux.
Solides compétences organisationnelles, avec une bonne maîtrise des tableurs et outils de présentation pour l’analyse, le suivi et la production de rapports.
Excellentes compétences en gestion des parties prenantes et en communication.
Maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais requise. La maîtrise du français constitue un atout majeur ; la connaissance d’autres langues européennes est appréciée.
Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles en anglais, notamment pour la rédaction de notes de synthèse, de résumés exécutifs et de propositions.
Autorisation légale de travailler en France requise.

Compétences et expérience souhaitées

Diplôme de niveau master ou équivalent en ingénierie, sciences, commerce, affaires internationales ou discipline connexe.
Bonne connaissance du paysage institutionnel spatial européen, notamment de la politique industrielle de l’ESA et des mécanismes de retour géographique.
Expérience avec un logiciel CRM ( Salesforce ou outil similaire) ainsi qu’avec des outils de recherche, de veille ou de constitution de listes de prospects/partenaires.

Exigences supplémentaires

Disponibilité pour des déplacements professionnels fréquents, jusqu’à 50 % du temps, principalement en Europe et ponctuellement au siège de Vast à Long Beach, dans le respect des règles applicables relatives au temps de travail et aux temps de repos.
Capacité à participer ponctuellement à des réunions en dehors des horaires habituels, afin de tenir compte des fuseaux horaires ou de soutenir des étapes critiques des missions, dans le respect de la législation applicable.

Vast is looking for a Project Manager, European Industrial Partnerships
to to lead the identification, development, and establishment of European industrial partnerships, and to provide programmatic and research leadership across Vast’s European human spaceflight and satellite activities. The Project Manager will report to the Director, Policy and Government Relations, and work in full coordination with the dedicated USA business development teams.

A central focus of this role is building the European industrial dimension of Vast’s offering: identifying European suppliers and partners whose capabilities align with Vast’s needs, and structuring partnerships that support geographical and industrial return considerations linked to flight seat opportunities and Vast’s broader procurement interests, in both the short and longer term.

Vast Europe is a small, nimble office, and this role is intentionally broad. You will work across research, partnerships, proposals, events, and project coordination, supporting both Directors. We consider this breadth a feature of the role. If you want a direct hand in how commercial human spaceflight deals with agencies, governments, and industry actually get built, and you are comfortable wearing multiple hats, this role is designed for you.

Key Responsibilities

Own and maintain a structured view of the European industrial landscape relevant to Vast: suppliers, capabilities, national strengths, and potential partners across member states.
Identify, develop, and help structure European industrial partnership opportunities that strengthen Vast’s offering to agency and government customers, including geographical and industrial return narratives supporting flight seat campaigns.
Conduct in-depth research on the European commercial space sector, including competitors, institutional programs, funding cycles, and regulatory developments, to identify opportunities and risks.
Prepare tailored research briefs, market intelligence, and background materials ahead of customer meetings, proposals, and negotiations.
Manage the preparation of proposals, offers, and responses to institutional tenders, including research, drafting, and coordination of inputs from Vast HQ teams and European partners.
Own CRM records, pipeline reporting, and internal tracking tools for the European team, and establish regular reporting processes.
Lead the planning and execution of Vast’s presence at European conferences, industry days, and customer events.
Provide project management across human spaceflight and satellite workstreams in support of both Directors, as priorities require.
Deputize for the Directors on industrial partnership and research matters as delegated, and support the onboarding and development of junior team members.

Candidate Profile

A curious, organized mid-career professional with substantive experience in the European space sector, strong research and writing skills, and the initiative to run down open questions independently. The ideal candidate is energized rather than intimidated by a broad remit, is comfortable owning workstreams end to end with limited supervision, and thrives with the autonomy and ambiguity of a small office backed by a fast-moving US headquarters.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, business, international affairs, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5–7 years of experience in the space industry, business development, industrial partnerships, procurement, or research and market intelligence roles.
Direct experience working with European industrial suppliers, primes, and/or institutional stakeholders.
Experience acting as a primary interface between a company or program and an external customer, at both technical and management levels.
Strong organizational skills and proficiency with spreadsheets and presentation tools for analysis and reporting.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
Fluency in English required. Fluency in French will be considered a strong plus. Fluency in other European languages appreciated
Strong written communication skills in English, including briefs, summaries, and proposal inputs.

jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, DC Power Utilization Management
jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
Experience with statistical analytics and programming languages such as R, Python, Ruby, etc.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
The Sr. Technical Strategy Analyst serves a critical role within the Command Action Group (CAG), providing direct, high-level support to the Program Director and Deputy Director of a major DoD acquisition program. This position requires a unique blend of technical expertise and executive-level strategic thinking. This role contributes to strategic research, assessments, data analysis, roadmap development, and the preparation of materials that support executive decision ‑ making for large-scale enterprise IT initiatives. Serving as the primary backup to the Technical Strategy Lead, the ideal candidate has strong analytical capabilities, can synthesize complex IT infrastructure information into clear insights, and is comfortable working in a fast ‑ paced CAG environment.

This role is on-site at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C.

An active Secret clearance is required.

Roles And Responsibilities

Strategy Analysis & Research

Conduct research and analysis on technology trends, capability gaps, and mission requirements related to enterprise IT environments and systems.
Evaluate emerging IT capabilities (e.g., cloud architectures, Zero Trust, DevSecOps, automation) for relevance to the acquisition program.
Develop summaries, insights, and recommendations that inform the Program Director's strategic direction.

Roadmap & Planning Support

Assist in developing multi ‑ year enterprise IT roadmaps, including sequencing, dependencies, and key acquisition milestones.
Maintain and update strategy artifacts, including concept papers, decision briefs, IT vision documents, and alignment frameworks.
Support the integration of technical strategy with engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and program management workstreams.

Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration

Partner with the Technical Strategy Lead to support workshops, working sessions, and leadership forums focused on enterprise IT strategy development and alignment.
Gather inputs from stakeholders across technical, operational, and business areas of the Program.
Consolidate feedback and help refine strategy recommendations based on stakeholder insights and acquisition program needs.
Serve as the designated alternate for the Technical Strategy Lead, representing the CAG and the Program Director's interests in senior-level technical and strategic forums during their absence.

Data Analysis & Insight Generation

Analyze qualitative and quantitative data related to IT service delivery, system performance, and enterprise technology adoption.
Develop charts, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate modernization trends, risks, and strategic opportunities.
Translate complex engineering and acquisition data into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership decision ‑ making.

Documentation & Executive Communication

Draft, synthesize, and refine strategy documents, white papers, decision briefs, and presentations for leadership evaluation.
Ensure technical IT materials are clear, concise, and tailored to senior audiences across classified and unclassified environments.

Job Requirements

Required Qualifications

Active Secret Clearance
7+ years of experience in strategy analysis, digital transformation, enterprise technology, or related analytical roles (Navy preferred).
Strong analytical, research, and problem ‑ solving skills.
Ability to synthesize complex technical and mission ‑ related information into concise insights.
Experience preparing executive-level briefs, reports, and visualizations.
Comfortable working collaboratively with technical, operational, and leadership stakeholders.
Ability to work in classified environments and handle sensitive information appropriately.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Systems Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a highly related technical discipline. Relevant experience (4+ years in addition to required) may be substituted for degree.
3+ years of demonstrated experience within DoD IT acquisition programs.
Advanced DAWIA certifications in Program Management or Engineering.
Familiarity with modern DoD IT initiatives, including DoD Zero Trust Architecture, Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC), and the Software Acquisition Pathway.

Amentum is seeking a Cybersecurity Analyst
to join our team and support our McLean, VA
customer. We are looking for team members who are passionate about making a difference by working on critical efforts we manage as a premier government contractor.

Our team is excited to help customers solve todays and tomorrow’s problems, giving confidence and reassurance that together we’ll accomplish mission success.

Purpose / Scope:

The Cybersecurity Analyst will perform assessment and authorization (A&A) efforts under the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) on behalf of a federal civilian agency as a contractor. The role will conduct cybersecurity analysis in preparation for A&A reviewing and validation of all associated cybersecurity documentation and technical controls.

The role will work within a team that conducts A&A activities. This individual will develop System Security Plans (SSP), Contingency Plans, Business Impact Analyses (BIA), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), Security Assessment Report (SARs), Security Assessment Plan (SAPs), and other RMF documentation.

This position covers all cybersecurity aspects including, but not limited to, identifying risks, validating the mitigation of plans of action, analyzing system designs, and assisting with A&A issues that may prevent a system from receiving authorization. It supports the implementation of RMF by developing documentation and updating policies, procedures, and processes as assigned.

The Cybersecurity Analyst will assess and mitigates system security threats/risks throughout the program life cycle. Contribute to the security planning, assessment, risk analysis, risk management, certification and awareness activities for system and networking operations. Create and review A&A Body of Evidence documentation, providing feedback on completeness and compliance of its content. Develop and execute Security Test Plan (STP) in close cooperation with team members. Manage and ensure Continuous Monitoring (CONMON) to maintain system authorization.

Essential Responsibilities:

Identify key stakeholders in A&A efforts and ensure system documentation reflects current system security configurations to include hardware and software components, data flow, interconnections, and ports, protocols, and services, etc.
Identify potential risks associated with system configurations and advise on mitigation strategies
Participate in A&A status meetings and facilitate moving systems toward a successful A&A effort
Assist to estimate Level of Effort (LOE) involved in performing A&A activities
Assist customer program offices in interpreting and applying mitigation strategies
Conduct thorough reviews of all vulnerabilities, architecture, and defense in depth strategies and report findings in POA&Ms document
Document residual risks and provide the cybersecurity risk analysis and mitigation determination results
Maintain cybersecurity policy and processes as assigned
Able to analyze, interpret, and apply Federal cybersecurity guidance to customer needs
Communicate the security posture of systems through designated reporting mechanism
Collaborate with other team members in cybersecurity

Minimum Requirements:

Experience developing A&A documentation from scratch and performing assessments; RMF step 1 through 4
Familiar with NIST publications, specifically RMF and NIST controls
One or more of the following certifications preferred (Security+, CAP, CISSP, CISM, GSEC, GCIH, or GSLC)
Minimum DoD 8570 Information Assurance Management Technology (IAM) level II
Familiar with dealing with defense-in-depth, and other information security and assurance principles and associated supporting technologies
Hands on experience and detailed familiarity with the A&A processes
Experience working in Xacta, Greenlight/Roadrunner
Excellent customer service and organization skills
Must demonstrate proficiency in the following areas: multi-tasking, critical thinking; and the ability to work quickly, efficiently and accurately in a dynamic and fluid environment
Must have a Top-Secret Clearance with polygraph
Must be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language

BA/BS Degree
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ability to interact and relay security technical requirements at all levels of leadership and work force
Ability to work both independently and as a member of a team

Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, occasional lifting to 20 pounds, constant sitting while using the computer terminal, constant use of sight abilities while reviewing documents, constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication, constant mental alertness, must possess planning/organizing skills, and must be able to work under deadlines.

Company Description

Digitas Health is the modern creative agency that takes on the biggest moments in healthcare
, raises the standard of creative, and connects people, partners, and ideas to create work that earns its place in culture. Purpose-built for today’s complex and evolving landscape, we partner with some of the world’s largest healthcare brands to do big things by moving faster, connecting deeper, and unlocking new possibilities at the intersection of creativity, data, technology, and empathy. Guided by our purpose, Connected for Good, and fueled by a vibrant, magnetic culture
—we deliver meaningful work that drives relevance, changes behavior, and creates lasting impact, always grounded in humanity, not just technology. As part of Publicis Health and Publicis Groupe
, we bring together entrepreneurial energy with the scale, stability, and depth of one of the world’s leading communications networks.

At Digitas Health, what sets us apart isn’t just who we work with, it’s how we work and how it feels to be here. Our culture attracts curious, driven people who want to make a difference and be part of something bigger.
Our teams are intentionally crafted across disciplines, perspectives, and experience levels, bringing strategy, creativity, data, and technology together from the start. We believe the best ideas come from curiosity, collaboration, and healthy debate and we expect people here to be thoughtful, engaged, and eager to shape what’s next. If you’re energized by complexity, motivated by impact, and excited to help redefine how healthcare connects with people, we’d love to meet you!

Overview

Project Managers independently lead projects across multiple workstreams, owning delivery from planning through completion while balancing scope, timing, budget, quality, and client expectations.

Project Managers bring clarity to complexity. They identify risks early, make informed decisions, manage competing priorities, and adjust plans before issues affect scope, cost, quality, or client confidence. They are trusted to own outcomes, navigate day-to-day trade-offs, and create confidence for teams, stakeholders, and clients through sound judgment and reliable execution.

As active delivery leaders, Project Managers apply strong project management, financial, and operational expertise to keep work moving forward, improve how work gets done, and strengthen delivery outcomes. They use new tools, technologies, and ways of working to improve visibility, efficiency, and delivery outcomes as client and business needs evolve.

Responsibilities

Strategy

Develop and manage project plans that establish a clear path to successful delivery across multiple workstreams.
Make day-to-day decisions that balance scope, timing, budget, quality, resource availability, and client needs.
Anticipate risks, trade-offs, and resource constraints early, adjusting plans and priorities to protect project outcomes.
Manage project scope and financial health proactively, identifying risks, evaluating options, and recommending solutions that support successful delivery and responsible business outcomes.
Lead discussions around priorities, resource needs, and delivery approaches, helping teams stay focused on the work that matters most.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, tools, and ways of working, applying changes that strengthen delivery outcomes and team effectiveness.

Delivery

Own successful delivery across multiple workstreams, ensuring work is completed on time, on budget, and at the expected level of quality.
Actively manage project scope, budgets, forecasts, timelines, and resource plans, identifying risks and opportunities early and driving solutions that support successful delivery and responsible business outcomes.
Monitor project health and delivery performance, proactively mitigating risks, addressing issues, and communicating impacts before they affect outcomes.
Manage scope changes, evolving priorities, and project constraints, helping teams understand implications, evaluate options, and move forward with clarity.
Lead cross-functional teams through delivery challenges, resolving dependencies, removing obstacles, and driving action to keep work moving forward.
Apply and evolve processes, tools, technologies, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve visibility, efficiency, execution quality, and delivery outcomes.

Knowledge

Apply project management, financial, and operational expertise to support sound delivery decisions and successful project outcomes.
Develop accurate estimates, scopes of work, budgets, forecasts, and resource plans that support effective planning and execution.
Apply financial and contractual knowledge to evaluate project health, identify risks early, and make recommendations that support responsible business outcomes.
Use project management platforms, workflow tools, and reporting to identify trends, inform decisions, and improve delivery performance.
Understand the business objectives behind the work and apply that context to delivery decisions, prioritization, and stakeholder discussions.
Evaluate and apply new tools, technologies, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve efficiency, visibility, and delivery outcomes.

Leadership

Build trust and confidence with teams, stakeholders, and clients through sound judgment, accountability, and follow-through.
Communicate project status, risks, decisions, and trade-offs clearly, distilling complex information into the key points teams and clients need to understand, so teams and clients understand what is happening, why it matters, and what comes next.
Manage client and stakeholder relationships proactively, addressing concerns early and maintaining confidence in delivery.
Own project outcomes by following issues through resolution and making the day-to-day decisions needed to keep work moving.
Bring forward practical recommendations, solutions, and next steps when teams need clarity or direction.
Use evolving tools, technologies, and ways of working to improve communication, collaboration, and delivery confidence.

Qualifications

What You Bring

3-5 years of agency, marketing, communications, healthcare, or related experience leading project delivery across multiple workstreams and stakeholders.
Strong project management and financial management skills, with the ability to balance scope, timing, budget, quality, and client needs.
Sound judgment and the confidence to make day-to-day decisions that keep work moving forward.
Strong communication and relationship management skills, with the ability to build alignment, navigate challenges, and create confidence with teams and clients.
A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to identify risks, evaluate options, and recommend a path forward.
Curiosity about new tools, technologies, and ways of working, with the ability to apply them to improve delivery outcomes.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

Additional Information

Our Publicis Groupe motto “Viva La Différence” means we’re better together, and we believe that our differences make us stronger. It means we honor and celebrate all identities, across all facets of intersectionality, and it underpins all that we do as an organization. We are focused on fostering belonging and creating equitable & inclusive experiences for all talent.

Publicis Groupe provides robust and inclusive benefit programs and policies to support the evolving and diverse needs of our talent and enable every person to grow and thrive. Our benefits package includes medical coverage, dental, vision, disability, 401K, as well as parental and family care leave, family forming assistance, tuition reimbursement, and flexible time off.

If you require accommodation or assistance with the application or onboarding process specifically, please contact USMTTACompliance@publicis.com.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on the skills, qualifications, and experience of the applicant along with the requirements of the position, and the Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time. Temporary roles may be eligible to participate in our freelancer/temporary employee medical plan through a third-party benefits administration system once certain criteria have been met. For regular roles, the Company will offer medical coverage, dental, vision, disability, 401k, and paid time off. new_jobs.title: Strategic Pre-Sales Program Manager - Security Systems Integration
