Overview

Kastle is a leader in premier property technology solutions, protecting everything from commercial real estate and global enterprises to critical government facilities and life-science labs. For over 50 years, we have provided safety to tens of thousands of businesses through state-of-the-art access control, video surveillance, and identity management. What makes us exceptional is our end-to-end approach to Managed Security as a Service. Because we engineer, install, monitor, and maintain our own systems, we are fully invested in their performance. Please visit Kastle Innovation to learn more about our solutions.

As the Pre-Sales Program Manager,
you are the single point of accountability for Kastle’s most complex Regional and National accounts. You will own the entire presales cycle from initial qualification through client acceptance. While you will not be doing technical design, you will act as a project leader uniting sales, engineering, subcontractors, and operations into a cohesive winning strategy. You will ensure every proposal is backed by a defined scope, schedule, and smooth operational handoff. To thrive here, you need strong program management experience and the executive presence to engage directly with ownership groups, developers, and enterprise clients.

Our success is driven by the combination of advanced technology and talented people. We are proud to be a Certified Great Place to Work®, recognized for a culture that prioritizes both professional excellence and employee well-being. In addition to a great work environment, we provide a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, and generous paid time off. Our offerings also include tuition and training assistance, BrightHorizons lifestyle assistance, life and disability insurance, and wellness programs. For more information on what it's like to work with us, please visit Life at Kastle.

Responsibilities

Strategic Pursuit Leadership

Serve as the overall pre-sales team leader for all Regional and National strategic account opportunities, coordinating the activities of sales engineers, solutions engineers, sub-contractors, and operations resources.
Partner with Strategic Account Managers to define client outcomes, establish win strategy, and shape the overall proposal approach.
Identify and define the full pre-sales resource requirements - people, skills, schedule, and budget needed to compete and win.
Lead client-facing outcome alignment sessions from initial qualification through go-live, ensuring client expectations are clearly defined and documented throughout.
Develop and maintain a detailed pre-sale project plan and pursuit strategy for each active strategic opportunity.

Proposal Development & Scope Ownership

Own the full proposal package for strategic pursuits: project scope of work, exclusions, preliminary project schedule (Gantt), sub-contractor RFQs and quotes, assumptions, and risk log.
Review sales engineering BOMs for completeness, dependencies, and unique site requirements; flag gaps prior to proposal submission.
Draft scope of work exclusions to protect Kastle from post-contract scope creep and change orders.
Ensure all proposal deliverables — drawings, BOMs, assumptions, pricing, and project schedule — are accurate, complete, and aligned with client requirements.
Lead large project reviews with sales and operations leadership on strategic opportunities to confirm scope, pricing model, and approval timeline.
Develop and deliver client presentation strategy for strategic pursuits; present with the account team when required.

Contract-to-Kickoff Transition

Own the contract-to-kickoff handoff- establishing the project channel, populating the project SharePoint folder (BOM, drawings, photos, sub quotes, outcome notes), and conducting a formal kickoff with the regional PM and Sales.
Develop the post-sale PM transition plan and ensure all project management continuity documentation is complete before transferring accountability to operations.
Identify post-sale project management involvement requirements and escalation protocols at proposal stage.

Post-Sale Oversight & Escalation

Co-own the Gantt chart with the regional PM during installation; update weekly and flag schedule risks to the National Account Manager before they reach the client.
Coordinate cross-functional dependencies — elevator vendors, GC schedules, turnstile sub-contractors, tenant provisioning, Kastle operations — to keep strategic projects on track.
Serve as the escalation point when operations encounters design ambiguity or scope questions during installation.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Serve as the connective layer between sales, sales engineering, solutions engineering, integrations, operations, and strategic sub-contractors throughout the pre-sales lifecycle.
Provide feedback to product and engineering teams on client needs, field integration challenges, and recurring proposal gaps.
Support development of client-specific marketing materials and executive-level presentations in partnership with the National Account Manager.

Qualifications

new_jobs.title: Strategic Business Manager/Strategic Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Strategic Business Manager owns one or more Strategic or Global Accounts of client organizations with scaled state, national, or global facilities and carries a personal revenue/quota and performance target tied to the account(s) assigned. This role leads a dedicated account team through the full account lifecycle: presale and solution development, design, contracting, and handoff for installation and maintenance, then stays accountable for the account's ongoing health and growth.

The account team led by the Strategic Business Program Manager fully represents the customer inside the company. The team develops the account, owns the sales process end to end, and is accountable for the quality and success of everything delivered against it, executing installation and service through the account's engineering and technical staff. The Strategic Business Manager does not simply oversee a sale; they own the customer's outcome from first contact through ongoing delivery. They manage a Team designed to represent the customer through sales, project management, admin and billing, and technical subject matter expertise tailored for the customer.

Scope scales with account size and complexity: a single large, complex account may require the Strategic Business Manager's full attention leading one team, while several smaller or less complex accounts may be grouped under one Strategic Business Manager leading multiple account teams. In either case, this role is the client's primary point of contact and the first line of leadership for their account team, reporting directly to the VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.

Organizational Structure & Team

Each account team led by the Strategic Business Manager is the customer's full representation inside the company — owning process, quality, and delivery outcomes, not just the initial sale. The team includes:

Account Executive or Account Manager: AE for developing accounts still building toward maturity; AM for mature, established accounts. Owns day-to-day sales motion and client relationship under this role's direction.
Administrator: Supports account operations, documentation, client-facing coordination, billing functions, scheduling, and coordination.
Project Manager or Project Coordinator: Owns project planning and execution once a sale moves into design and contracting. Handles presale and post sale due to multiple stakeholders and potentially long sales cycles. PM/PC is also ensuring communication and deliverables are customized and dedicated specifically for the customer.
Systems Technician: Coordinates with internal and external engineering and technical staff and the dedicated technical delivery team to execute installation and service, and is accountable for the quality of that delivery. The Systems Technician will be an SME (Subject Matter Expert) to ensure success, customer needs are communicated and met, and forecast planning and needs on behalf of the customer.

Roles & Responsibilities

Account Ownership & Customer Representation

Fully represent the customer inside and outside the company: own the account's process, quality, and delivery outcomes from first contact through ongoing service, not just the initial sale.
Carry a personal revenue/quota and performance target across assigned account(s); own forecasting and pipeline accuracy for those accounts.
Own the client relationship at multiple levels for assigned accounts, ensuring the account's strategy aligns with client objectives and company capacity.
Identify and pursue expansion, renewal, and cross-sell opportunities within existing accounts.
Work with leadership and vendor peers for solutions and strategies.

Sales Process & Delivery Oversight

Own the sales process for assigned accounts from opportunity through contracting, including proposal development and pricing decisions within approved authority.
Oversee handoff from contracting into design, installation, and maintenance, ensuring the account team and the account's engineering and technical staff are aligned on scope, schedule, and quality.
Own the quality of everything delivered against the account, working through the Systems Technician and engineering/technical staff to execute installation and service to standard.
Monitor project and service delivery performance against SLA and client expectations for assigned accounts.

Team Leadership

Directly manage the Account Executive/Account Manager, Administrator, Project Manager/Coordinator, and Systems Technician assigned to each account team.
Set individual and team performance expectations; coach, develop, and provide day-to-day direction.
Recommend hiring, staffing, and structure changes for account teams as accounts grow or shift in complexity.

Escalation & Cross-Functional Coordination

Serve as first point of escalation for client, delivery, or internal issues within assigned accounts; resolve directly or engage the appropriate internal team.
Escalate issues beyond this role's authority, cross-departmental blockers, resourcing conflicts, or client-relationship risk to the Director or VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.
Coordinate with other Strategic Business Managers and the dedicated technical delivery team to maintain consistent quality and process across the division.

Reporting

Provide regular account health, adopted portfolio, total solution targets, pipeline, and delivery status reporting to the Director or VP, Global & Strategic Accounts.
Maintain accurate account and opportunity data in CRM/ERP systems used by the division.
P&L Responsibilities
Utilization, AHR (Avg Hourly Rates), Margin, and other assigned leading or lagging indicators

Education And/or Experience

5+ years in strategic/enterprise account management or sales leadership, with a track record of carrying and meeting quota.
Experience managing multi-site or multi-facility client relationships (20+ locations preferred) from sale through delivery.
Experience directly managing a multi-disciplinary team (sales, project management, technical/field coordination roles).
Experience in systems integration, security, telecommunications, or a related technical products/services industry preferred.
Comfortable owning escalations and coordinating across departments to resolve client-impacting issues.
Familiarity with CRM/ERP and project/service management systems.
Willingness to travel to client sites as required by assigned accounts.

Company Overview

Day Wireless Systems is the largest full-service wireless integrator in the West. We provide design, construction, licensing, sales, service, rentals, installation, and maintenance for a wide range of wireless voice, data, and video applications.

Founded in 1969, today we have 30 locations and 400+ employees in California, Oregon, Washington, Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Day Wireless employees enjoy the opportunity to grow and transfer within our many locations and business divisions.

Moses Lake Industries, Inc. (MLI) is a rapidly growing producer of ultra-pure chemical products, serving the semiconductor and flat-panel screen industries worldwide. We deliver world class products to the leaders of the industries we serve.

You will be working for a midsized company with great people and a history of steady growth and profitability. Sound like a match? If you are prepared to work in an exciting and rewarding environment, we look forward to considering your experience and qualifications.

Shift/Hours/Location:
M-F, 8am-5pm, Onsite/Hybrid, Moses Lake, WA

What You Will Be Working On

End-to-End Product Oversight: Manage and coordinate all aspects of multiple technical products, including product development, market analysis, supply chain optimization, cost structure evaluation, and profitability assessment.
Product Vision & Strategy: Define product vision, strategy, and roadmap. Gather, manage, and prioritize market and customer requirements while providing guidance and support to the program management team.
Financial Performance Management: Actively manage Profit & Loss, including cost structure, pricing strategies, and other key performance indicators (KPIs).
Product Development & Improvement: Develop and execute strategies for new product development (NPD) and continuous product improvement.
Program Advisory: Acts as advisor to the program team on project tasks and operations
Requirements Definition: Establish detailed product requirements, including specifications and metrology standards.
Strategic Planning: Create, own, and continuously refine product strategies and tactical plans to ensure alignment with business objectives.
Market Research & Analysis: Conduct global market research to assess capacity, supply-demand dynamics, and pricing trends for effective product marketing.
Customer-Centric Innovation: Define customer requirements for next-generation products to drive innovation and competitiveness.
Phase Gate Reviews: Lead and approve all tasks and deliverables for Phase 0 and Phase 1, and review/approve subsequent Phase Gate Reviews (PGR).
Business Case Development: Develop and realize comprehensive business cases to support product initiatives and strategic investments.
Costing Oversight: Approve costing/proposed pricing and assist with complex requests, including new warehousing solutions and shipping challenges.
Forecast Validation: Run and validate forecasting models to ensure accuracy and alignment with business objectives.
Customer Requirements Review: Assess new customer requirements, coordinate with internal teams, and identify process improvements or gaps necessary to meet customer expectations.
Strategic Alignment: Drive product and customer strategy, ensuring clear communication and alignment across internal stakeholder groups while troubleshooting issues.
Escalation Management: Handle Level 3 customer escalations and OCAP (Out-of-Control Action Plan) support, including preparation of escalation materials, participation in OCAP meetings as needed, and coordination with TM, PM, AM, QA, and QC teams for responses.
Cost Reduction Initiatives: Develop and implement cost reduction strategies to optimize profitability.
Continuous Improvement: Lead planning and execution of continuous improvement initiatives across processes and operations.
Audit Participation: Support major customer audits and provide ongoing assistance for corrective action responses.
Collaborating with Senior Planning Manager in costing and pricing for new products and/or customers (including location), including review with AM, support for PM/PLM
FSC for new product lines/packaging changes for owned RFQs
Initiate and/or Drive MOCs related to plant-wide changes, major expansions, or customer-sensitive changes (bulk sulfuric, building expansion, etc.).
Provide customer requirements for all MOCs. Final approver on closure of MOCs.
Costing & Pricing Management: Collaborate with Senior Planning Manager in costing and pricing for new products and/or customers, including location-specific considerations. Collaborate with Account Managers (AM) and provide support to Program Managers (PM) and Product Lifecycle Managers (PLM).
Financial Structure Control (FSC): Collaborate with Senior Planning Manager in FSC activities for new product lines and packaging changes related to owned RFQs.

Strict compliance with Environmental and Safety regulations.

Experience with New Product Development (NPD) processes and stage-gate methodologies.
Experience developing and presenting business cases to senior leadership for strategic investment decisions.

Management of Change (MOC) process expertise, particularly for plant-wide or customer-sensitive changes.
Product Change Notification (PCN) preparation and management.

Strategic planning & road mapping: Ability to define product vision, strategy, and roadmaps.
Data-driven decision making: Ability to leverage KPIs and dashboards for performance management.

Escalation management: Composure and skill in handling customer escalations and OCAP processes.
Stakeholder communication: Clear, strategic communication to ensure alignment across internal groups.
Advisory & mentoring capability: Serving as an advisor to the program team on tasks and operations.
Audit readiness: Experience supporting major customer audits and driving corrective action responses.
Professionalism: Consistent demonstration of professionalism in appearance, conduct, and attitude.
Working knowledge of computers and MS Office software.
Working knowledge of arithmetic and grammar.

Manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously to meet established deadlines.
Work as a team and/or independently.
Perform tasks with attention to detail and accuracy.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.

Experience in high-purity chemical manufacturing environments.

new_jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
Experience with statistical analytics and programming languages such as R, Python, Ruby, etc.

new_jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers

Our customers are the frontier labs. You'll work alongside the people building the models everyone else is reading about, on the problems they haven't solved yet, and what you ship becomes part of how they decide whether an agent is safe to release. Very few roles put you that close to the frontier.

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own those projects. You'll run several lab engagements at once, each with its own researchers, engineers, and reviewers. You decide who works on what, you hold the schedule, and you decide whether a batch is good enough to ship.
The field is cutting-edge, and the projects change shape faster than any playbook can describe.

What you'll do

Project ownership

Own concurrent lab engagements end-to-end: scope, milestones, delivery, and status
Turn a customer specification into a task plan with your researchers and engineers: how many tasks, in which environments, against which models, by when
Track every batch through the pipeline (in progress, under review, approved, delivered) and keep the delivery record accurate enough that anyone can read the state of a project in a minute
Surface a slipping deadline early, with the tradeoff already worked out: cut scope, add capacity, or move the date

Researcher allocation and quality

Allocate researchers, task writers, and reviewers across projects based on throughput and specialty
Own their onboarding: brief them on the environment, the attack pattern, and the acceptance criteria, then get them to their first accepted task fast
Give quality feedback on rejected work and spot the patterns behind repeat rejections
Manage the review chain so that no batch reaches the customer before it has cleared internal review

What we're looking for

2 to 4 years in project management, program management, or product management, in a role where you owned a delivery and not just a workstream
High autonomy in an undefined space. The right answer to “what's the process for this?” is usually that you write it
Comfortable managing contributors you don't line-manage: setting expectations, giving direct feedback, and making the call when quality doesn't come up
Fluent written and spoken English

Advantage

A technical background: industrial engineering, computer science, information systems, or equivalent hands-on experience
Exposure to LLMs or AI agents, whether professional or self-taught
Background in security, red teaming, or trust and safety
Experience coordinating a distributed or contract contributor team
Data fluency: SQL, spreadsheets, or scripting well enough to answer your own questions about project throughput

Alice is a trust, safety, and security company built for the AI era. We safeguard the communicative technologies people use to create, collaborate, and interact- whether with each other or with machines.

In a world where AI has fundamentally changed the nature of risk, Alice provides end-to-end coverage across the entire AI lifecycle. We support frontier model labs, enterprises, and UGC platforms with a comprehensive suite of solutions: from model hardening evaluations and pre-deployment red-teaming to runtime guardrails and ongoing drift detection.

Alice is widely considered a global leader in online safety and AI security. We have some of the most forward-thinking and passionate minds in the world working to safeguard over 3 billion users across the largest AI and tech platforms.

This Sr. Program Manager role will lead a program within Financial Integrity Trust (FIT), a team embedded within the Financial Risk Mitigation (FRM) organization. The Business Operations Analyst, Physical Security I supports operational excellence across Physical Security by monitoring key security processes, analyzing operational data, and identifying opportunities to improve security effectiveness, compliance, and service delivery. This role partners with internal stakeholders, contract security providers, and other vendors to support day-to-day security operations. new_jobs.title: Epidemiology Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Amentum is seeking a driven and professional Epidemiology Operations Senior Analyst
to work on the PACOM Command Surgeon’s (J07) Decision Support Team (DST). This position serves as the DST's senior expert for infectious-disease surveillance, population-health trends, and epidemiological risk, acting as a primary liaison with civilian health agencies, academia, and foreign partners. The Analyst leads wastewater-based epidemiology and integrates public health, biosurveillance, wastewater, open-source, operational, and classified information to identify anomalies and assess force-health and mission effects. General public health experience without applied epidemiological or biosurveillance expertise is insufficient. Assigned to J85, the position directly supports J07, entails hybrid work from Camp Smith and other local locations, receives functional priorities from J07 through established contract channels, operates with project and technical oversight from J85, and reports administratively to the Amentum Project Lead.

Essential Responsibilities
:

Analyze epidemiological, public-health, wastewater, biosurveillance, operational, open-source, and classified information to identify trends, anomalies, clusters, and emerging threats.
Lead wastewater-surveillance baseline, indicator, trend, and anomaly-threshold development with laboratory, public-health, and CBRNE specialists.
Assess the significance, reliability, limitations, uncertainty, and operational implications of epidemiological findings.
Provide findings to the Operations Planner for integration with medical intelligence, CBRNE analysis, Force Health Protection, and operational plans.
Monitor emerging infectious diseases and public-health threats across the US PACOM AOR using DoW, interagency, state, foreign-government, and partner data.
Support epidemiological investigations and assessments in coordination with authorized DoW medical and public-health personnel.
Coordinate with J07, subordinate commands, theater public-health organizations, overseas laboratories, intelligence analysts, military planners, and external partners.
Test the Biosurveillance Information Platform and provide epidemiology-specific findings for Military Utility Assessments and recommendations.
Translate surveillance needs into requirements for technical teams developing feeds, dashboards, alerts, and workflows; coding is not required.
Develop surveillance protocols, data-quality standards, analytic methods, reports, white papers, and capability-improvement recommendations.

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's degree or higher in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health science, or a closely related discipline.
Must have an active Secret security clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance.
7+ years of progressively responsible experience in epidemiology, public health surveillance, disease monitoring, outbreak analysis, or a related field.
Experience independently analyzing complex surveillance data and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Knowledge of epidemiological design, surveillance methods, statistical concepts, disease-activity measures, data quality, and uncertainty.
Familiarity with military planning and ability to work with military planners, intelligence professionals, technical teams, and decision-makers.
Strong writing, consultation, coordination, and senior-leader briefing skills.
Active Top-Secret security clearance, with SCI eligibility later during employment.
Master of Public Health or another relevant master's degree; wastewater-based epidemiology experience.
DoW, Combatant Command, public-health agency, or infectious-disease surveillance experience.
Knowledge of microbiology, pathophysiology, syndromic surveillance, and emerging diseases.
Indo-Pacific experience and familiarity with AI-enabled tools, Maven Smart System, or biosurveillance platforms.

Compensation & Benefits

HIRING SALARY RANGE: $165K - $180K (Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant internal equity, and alignment with market data.)

This position includes a competitive benefits package. For more detailed information on our Benefits and what it is like to work for Amentum: please visit our careers site: www.amentumcareers.com

$165K - $180K

Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as job responsibilities, education, experience, skills, internal equity, market data, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and relevant laws.

Your expertise will directly impact how we serve clients across borders, and report risk information to senior management, making you an essential part of a diverse, high-performing team that values innovation, integrity, and continuous learning.

This is a full-time, on-site role, working Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Responsibilities

Production of non-financial risk reports used for management information risk oversight.
Derivation of DBS RCSA inputs based on outsourced activities. Contribution to the determination of Important Business Services and Operational Resilience aspects.
Derivation of quantitative metrics required for regulatory reporting and supervisory purposes.
Determination of market purity and cross border training assignment and Use of In app to check cross border samples.
Contribute to the derivation of Non-Financial Risk controls.

Skills

2+ years in Non-Financial Risk within Private Banking, with strong knowledge of IT skills (specifically Excel) banking documentation and regulations.
Outstanding analytical skills to assess and interpret complex excel files.
Solid understanding of private banking products, services and international regulatory requirements.
Excellent problem-solving skills, multitasking, attention to detail and accuracy, with strong teamwork and organizational skills, with ability to work under strict deadlines.
Excellent spoken and written English; additional languages (e.g., French, German) are an advantage.
Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimise workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs.

new_jobs.title: Interdisciplinary Statistician (Economics )/Economist/Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist)
new_jobs.description:
Summary

This position is part of the Defense Human Resources Activity (Personnel Readiness Management Agency) . The incumbent Serves in a developmental training interdisciplinary position as a Statistician (Economics),Economist, or Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) assisting in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances and providing support with managing certain aspects of the BAH, OHA, Overseas COLA, and CONUS COLA programs.

Learn More About This Agency

Duties

Help

As a Interdisciplinary Statistician (Economics )/Economist/Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) At The GS-0110/1515/1530-7/9/11/12 Some Of Your Typical Work Assignments May Include

GS-7

Serves in a developmental capacity, assisting senior analysts in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances (BAH, OHA, COLA).
With close supervision, analyzes housing and cost-of-living data to help produce rate recommendations.
Assists in researching economic issues and reviewing data reports and statistical summaries to support rate suggestions.
Helps prepare reports, memorandums, and allowance materials for publication and dissemination.
Assists the team in responding to inquiries regarding allowance programs and survey results.

GS-9

Independently carries out recurring assignments to develop and analyze military housing and cost-of-living surveys.
Analyzes statistical and economic data to produce allowance rate recommendations in conformance with accepted policies.
Conducts in-depth reviews of data reports and statistical summaries, identifying and researching economic issues and facts for allowance determinations.
Prepares recommendations, reports, and responses to customer inquiries on allowance programs with limited supervisory review.
Designs and builds user-focused analytics to extract actionable information from diverse data sources to inform decision-makers.

GS-11

Plans and conducts a variety of complex studies on housing and cost-of-living programs, resolving difficult issues and interpreting policy.
Independently analyzes and defends rate-setting methodologies and makes recommendations that have a significant impact on service members.
Develops and refines analytical methods and procedures for data collection, validation, and the accomplishment of surveys.
Serves as a technical resource, providing professional assistance and advice to the Department on allowance programs.
Prepares and presents detailed briefings, complex analyses, and justifications for multiple audiences to defend findings and program recommendations.

GS-12

Serves as a senior analyst and subject matter expert responsible for the full lifecycle of developing, analyzing, and managing allowance programs.
Leads the most complex and critical analyses of economic and statistical data, formulating and defending final rate recommendations for senior leadership approval.
Presents and defends allowance programs and rate-setting methodologies against challenges and public scrutiny, representing the agency in high-level meetings.
Develops and implements new analytical techniques and criteria to improve program effectiveness and advises management on long-range plans and objectives.
Provides authoritative guidance and mentorship to junior analysts and coordinates with high-ranking officials across DoD, government agencies, and private sources.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

Must be a U.S. citizen
Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service
Resume and supporting documents (See How To Apply)
Suitable for Federal employment, determined by a background investigation
May be required to successfully complete a probationary period
Work Schedule: Full Time
Overtime: Occasionally
Tour of Duty: Flexible
Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized
Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA): Non-Exempt
Financial Disclosure: Not Required
Telework Eligibility: This position is telework eligible
This position may require occasional travel, as conditions allow.
This position is Noncritical-Sensitive, requiring a Secret clearance.

Qualifications

You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service:
Applying advanced statistical, economic, or operations-research principles to analyze and evaluate allowance-program issues and provide technical expertise on allowance programs.
Leading complex analytical projects involving the development or substantial revision of data-collection approaches, analytical techniques, or program-evaluation criteria.
Developing, presenting, and defending recommendations and analytical methodologies for complex allowance-program issues before senior officials, stakeholders, oversight bodies, or other public-facing audiences.

OR

Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree.

You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service:
Conducting comprehensive analyses of complex data using advanced statistical, economic, or data-science analytical and evaluative methods, and developing recommendations based on the results.
Modifying or adapting standard data-science and statistical techniques to address a range of analytical challenges, program issues, or policy questions.
Planning and carrying out complex studies, documenting and justifying findings, and presenting results to technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior officials.

OR

Master's or equivalent graduate degree.

You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service:
Applying established statistical, economic, or data-science methods to analyze and evaluate data for routine projects or assignments.
Independently using automated analytical tools, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar software, to extract, organize, and analyze information from complex data sources.
Resolving conventional problems in data collection and analysis by applying established program methodologies, procedures, and regulations.

OR

2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree.

OR

Possess some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and have more than one year of graduate level education as described, but less than two. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%.

You may qualify at the GS-07, if you fulfill the following qualifications:

One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service:
Assisting with developmental assignments by applying statistical, economic, or data-science principles, methods, and techniques under guidance.
Using automated systems and software, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar tools, to access, retrieve, organize, and review data from multiple sources.
Assisting with research, interpretation, and evaluation of data using qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for well-precedented assignments.

OR

Possess: a Bachelor's degree w/Superior Academic Achievement or 1 year of graduate level education.

OR

Have some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and I have some but less than one year of graduate level education as described. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%.

In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0110/1515/1530 series.

If you are applying for the Economist0110 series, you must have the following.
Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus.
OR
Combination of education and experience courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education.
If you are applying for the Operations Research 1515 series, you must have the following.
Degree: in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics, Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science, optimization; mathematical modeling; queueing theory; engineering; physics (except descriptive or survey courses); econometrics; psychometrics; biometrics; experimental psychology; physical chemistry; industrial process analysis; managerial economics; computer science; measurement for management; mathematical models in social phenomena; and courses that involved application of operations research techniques and methodologies to problems of management, marketing, systems design, and other specialized fields; or other comparable quantitative analysis courses. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus.
If you are applying for the Statistics 1530 series, you must have the following.
Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing.
OR
Combination of education and experience courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position.

Education

Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

ARE YOU USING YOUR EDUCATION TO QUALIFY? You MUST provide transcripts or other documentation to support your educational claims.

All materials must be submitted by the closing date of the announcement.

new_jobs.title: Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Implement risk management processes at the ground level for the construction finance business, gaining a thorough understanding of the project and developer and preparing a credit memo to assess the project viability and proposal structure as per ABHFL risk parameters and customer requirements. Key activities are analysis of project viability, assessment of market information and developer financials.

Job Context & Major Challenges

Job Context/ Job Challenges

Job Context

Key Aspects

The company has a well-defined vision of being one of the most reputed and material financiers within the lending space-spread across both retail HNI and corporate clientele. We have made significant investments in our process and system infrastructure towards preparing for the next level of growth and are one of the only financial entities certified for ISO 9001:2008 across all our business processes. Spread across 18 cities, we plan on further diversifying our risk and revenue mix through expansion into new geographies and new product segments allowing our customers a one-window shop for all their financing needs.

The Business Credit Analyst is an integral part of the Construction Finance Business and is responsible for analyzing the proposals with the required due diligence and to ensure that all information required to take a credit decision is captured in the proposal.

The analyst is also responsible to ensure that proposals are compliant with all the norms of credit policy, RBI regulations and other statutory regulations.

He/she has to maintain stipulated TAT in credit appraisal process and is also responsible for keeping update on the various changes in economic scenario, sectors, etc., co-ordination with sales team and RMG for faster decisions to improvise TATs of the overall sanction process.

Market Intelligence and understanding Competition best practices and suggesting changes in the existing product / policy and processes.

Generating various MISs and EWS (early warning signals), overall portfolio monitoring form risk as well as compliance perspective is an important job aspect.

Key Challenges

Cross functional coordination to enable timely approval of credit proposals

Self-updating on economic / sectoral changes in the economy

Improvising on TAT

Seamless co-ordination with multiple internal and external entities

New product development

Enabling Skill Sets & Qualifications

The critical skill sets are a strong analytical acumen, evaluation skills, detail orientation & decision-making skills, initiative & target orientation & market intelligence developed through a strong industry network.

The education & experience required to fulfil this profile are a Chartered Accountant or an MBA with minimum 2-4 years of experience in credit and risk functions of Banks/NBFCs.

Key Result Areas

KRA (Accountabilities) (Max 1325 Characters)
Supporting Actions (Max 1325 Characters)

KRA1 To Assess and conduct detailed credit analysis & evaluation of lending proposals for approval / decision at the local level or further recommendation for approval/ decision to Risk team for further approval at CC level Meet with developers and builders to understand the viability of their projects, in terms of project scale, progress and financials. Provide inputs towards the structuring of the deal, ensuring compliance with internal risk and external regulatory requirements. Carry out an analysis of the balance sheet and recent financial results of developers and their organizations. Carry out background research on the project, the developer and the regional market, highlighting any negative reports so as to ensure the quality of ABHFLs lending portfoli. To interact with the Legal and Technical agencies to ensure that property risk have been understood and mitigated. Monitor statutory real estate guidelines and assess any relevant information from these sources

KRA2 Emphasize strict compliance and adherence to internal risk management and external regulatory norms Ensure a thorough understanding and acceptance of the ABFL credit risk strategies, and ensure that appropriate credit risk parameters are incorporated in proposals. To work with the Central Risk teams to identify risk areas and build processes to mitigate risk, including performance metrics and documented procedures. Monitor customer accounts on a periodic basis to ensure the maintenance of acceptable asset quality levels. Track delinquent and potentially problematic accounts closely, taking action to minimize the level of NPAs within the region.

KRA3 Vendor Management Identifying and recommendation for Appointment of vendors at local levels including valuation, legal, Field Investigation Agencies, Fraud Containment Agencies. Managing TAT with various vendors- a) Field investigation, b) Lawyers, c) Technical Valuers, d) RCU agency to ensure Customer Delight. Regular Training and reviewing the performance of the vendors with regular interaction and keeping eye on the other financial institution association.

KRA4 Process Management Ensuring that end to end processes are followed as per the SOPs as defined for CF at the local assessment level. Continuous improvement in credit approval process to meet the dynamic business needs and instituting mechanisms for adherence of risk associated with the product s, safety of financed amount and customer satisfaction. Proper capturing of data in the requisite system to ensure proper MIS generation for business decisions. Training implementation for Local Credit Process team, Sales team on product, processes, legal and technical aspects. Handling customer escalations and complaints during and post disbursements -replies to mailers, correspondences with co-ordination with the legal team

new_jobs.title: Project Manager, European Industrial Partnerships | Chef de projet, Partenariats Européens industriels et Stratégiques
new_jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure
using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite
, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California
, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast recherche un(e) Chef de projet – Partenariats industriels et Stratégiques
, rattaché(e) au Directeur des Politiques Publiques et des Relations Gouvernementales.

Le/la titulaire du poste aura pour mission d’identifier, de développer et de mettre en place des partenariats industriels européens, ainsi que d’assurer le pilotage de projets et de travaux de recherche liés aux activités de Vast en matière de vols spatiaux habités et de satellites en Europe. Il/elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes américaines de développement commercial.

L’un des principaux objectifs de ce poste sera de développer la dimension industrielle européenne de l’offre de Vast : identifier les fournisseurs et partenaires européens dont les capacités répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise, et structurer des partenariats soutenant les considérations de retour géographique et industriel associées aux opportunités institutionnelles, aux attributions de sièges et aux besoins d’approvisionnement plus larges de Vast, à court comme à long terme.

Vast Europe est une structure agile à taille humaine, et ce poste est volontairement polyvalent. Le/la titulaire contribuera aux travaux de recherche, au développement de partenariats, à la préparation de propositions, à l’organisation d’événements et à la coordination de projets, en appui aux deux directeurs.

Cette polyvalence constitue un élément central du poste. Si vous souhaitez participer concrètement au développement des vols spatiaux habités commerciaux, en collaboration avec les agences, les gouvernements et l’industrie, et que vous êtes à l’aise dans la gestion simultanée de plusieurs projets, ce poste est fait pour vous.

Il s’agit d’un poste à temps plein, en CDI, basé dans notre bureau de Paris, siège européen de Vast. Rémunération selon profil et expérience.

Principales responsabilités

Développer et maintenir une vision structurée de l’écosystème industriel européen pertinent pour Vast : fournisseurs, capacités, expertises nationales, pôles de compétences et partenaires potentiels dans les États membres.
Identifier, développer et contribuer à structurer des opportunités de partenariats industriels européens renforçant l’offre de Vast auprès des agences et clients gouvernementaux, notamment au travers d’arguments liés au retour géographique et industriel dans le cadre des campagnes d’attribution de sièges.
Mener des analyses approfondies du secteur spatial commercial européen, incluant les concurrents, programmes institutionnels, cycles de financement, évolutions réglementaires et dynamiques de marché, afin d’identifier les opportunités et les risques.
Préparer des notes de recherche ciblées, études de marché et documents de référence en amont des réunions clients, des propositions et des négociations.
Gérer la préparation des propositions, offres et réponses aux appels d’offres institutionnels, incluant la recherche, la rédaction et la coordination des contributions des équipes du siège de Vast et des partenaires européens.
Gérer les données CRM, les rapports de pipeline et les outils de suivi internes pour l’équipe européenne, et mettre en place des processus réguliers de reporting.
Piloter la planification et l’exécution de la présence de Vast lors de conférences européennes, journées sectorielles et événements clients.
Assurer la gestion de projets liés aux vols spatiaux habités et aux activités satellitaires, en appui aux deux directeurs et selon les priorités définies.
Assurer, selon les délégations reçues, l’intérim des directeurs sur les sujets liés aux partenariats industriels et à la recherche, et contribuer à l’intégration ainsi qu’au développement des membres juniors de l’équipe.

Profil du candidat

Professionnel(le) confirmé(e), curieux(se), rigoureux(se) et organisé(e), disposant d’une solide connaissance du secteur spatial européen, d’excellentes compétences en recherche et en rédaction, ainsi que d’une capacité avérée à conduire des analyses de manière autonome.
Le/la candidat(e) idéal(e) est motivé(e) par un large éventail de responsabilités, sait gérer des projets de bout en bout avec un niveau limité de supervision, et s’épanouit dans un environnement agile, autonome et parfois imprévisible, propre à une petite structure européenne adossée à un siège américain dynamique.

Compétences et expérience requises

Diplôme de niveau licence ou supérieur en ingénierie, sciences, commerce, affaires internationales ou discipline connexe.
5 à 7 ans d’expérience minimum dans le secteur spatial, le développement commercial, les partenariats industriels, les achats, ou des fonctions liées à la recherche et à l’intelligence de marché.
Expérience directe avec des fournisseurs industriels européens, maîtres d’œuvre et/ou acteurs institutionnels.
Expérience avérée en tant qu’interface principale entre une entreprise ou un programme et un client externe, tant sur les aspects techniques que managériaux.
Solides compétences organisationnelles, avec une bonne maîtrise des tableurs et outils de présentation pour l’analyse, le suivi et la production de rapports.
Excellentes compétences en gestion des parties prenantes et en communication.
Maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais requise. La maîtrise du français constitue un atout majeur ; la connaissance d’autres langues européennes est appréciée.
Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles en anglais, notamment pour la rédaction de notes de synthèse, de résumés exécutifs et de propositions.
Autorisation légale de travailler en France requise.

Diplôme de niveau master ou équivalent en ingénierie, sciences, commerce, affaires internationales ou discipline connexe.
Bonne connaissance du paysage institutionnel spatial européen, notamment de la politique industrielle de l’ESA et des mécanismes de retour géographique.

Vast is looking for a Project Manager, European Industrial Partnerships
to to lead the identification, development, and establishment of European industrial partnerships, and to provide programmatic and research leadership across Vast’s European human spaceflight and satellite activities. The Project Manager will report to the Director, Policy and Government Relations, and work in full coordination with the dedicated USA business development teams.

A central focus of this role is building the European industrial dimension of Vast’s offering: identifying European suppliers and partners whose capabilities align with Vast’s needs, and structuring partnerships that support geographical and industrial return considerations linked to flight seat opportunities and Vast’s broader procurement interests, in both the short and longer term.

Vast Europe is a small, nimble office, and this role is intentionally broad. You will work across research, partnerships, proposals, events, and project coordination, supporting both Directors. We consider this breadth a feature of the role. If you want a direct hand in how commercial human spaceflight deals with agencies, governments, and industry actually get built, and you are comfortable wearing multiple hats, this role is designed for you.

Key Responsibilities

Own and maintain a structured view of the European industrial landscape relevant to Vast: suppliers, capabilities, national strengths, and potential partners across member states.
Identify, develop, and help structure European industrial partnership opportunities that strengthen Vast’s offering to agency and government customers, including geographical and industrial return narratives supporting flight seat campaigns.
Conduct in-depth research on the European commercial space sector, including competitors, institutional programs, funding cycles, and regulatory developments, to identify opportunities and risks.
Prepare tailored research briefs, market intelligence, and background materials ahead of customer meetings, proposals, and negotiations.
Manage the preparation of proposals, offers, and responses to institutional tenders, including research, drafting, and coordination of inputs from Vast HQ teams and European partners.
Own CRM records, pipeline reporting, and internal tracking tools for the European team, and establish regular reporting processes.
Lead the planning and execution of Vast’s presence at European conferences, industry days, and customer events.
Provide project management across human spaceflight and satellite workstreams in support of both Directors, as priorities require.
Deputize for the Directors on industrial partnership and research matters as delegated, and support the onboarding and development of junior team members.

Candidate Profile

A curious, organized mid-career professional with substantive experience in the European space sector, strong research and writing skills, and the initiative to run down open questions independently. The ideal candidate is energized rather than intimidated by a broad remit, is comfortable owning workstreams end to end with limited supervision, and thrives with the autonomy and ambiguity of a small office backed by a fast-moving US headquarters.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, business, international affairs, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5–7 years of experience in the space industry, business development, industrial partnerships, procurement, or research and market intelligence roles.
Direct experience working with European industrial suppliers, primes, and/or institutional stakeholders.
Experience acting as a primary interface between a company or program and an external customer, at both technical and management levels.
Strong organizational skills and proficiency with spreadsheets and presentation tools for analysis and reporting.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
Fluency in English required. Fluency in French will be considered a strong plus. Fluency in other European languages appreciated
Strong written communication skills in English, including briefs, summaries, and proposal inputs.

new_jobs.title: Lead Client Program Manager, Pricing and Reference Data
new_jobs.description:
FactSet creates flexible, open data and software solutions for over 200,000 investment professionals worldwide, providing instant access to financial data and analytics that investors use to make crucial decisions.

At FactSet, our values are the foundation of everything we do. They express how we act and operate, serve as a compass in our decision-making, and play a big role in how we treat each other, our clients, and our communities. We believe that the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere, at any time, and that curiosity is the key to anticipating our clients’ needs and exceeding their expectations.

Your Team's Impact

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated individual to join our Data Solutions group as a Program Manager working with Pricing and Reference Data (PRD) clients.

The Data Solutions group is responsible for the growth of FactSet’s DataFeed (off-platform) products and solutions. Our aim is to consult & organize our client’s data consumption processes with FactSet proprietary and industry standard delivery solutions. As a Program Manager in APAC, you will draw on your understanding of the region’s regulatory, cultural, and language considerations to tailor project delivery and ensure efficient, impactful client engagement across multiple countries.

Pricing and Reference Data is foundational data used to identify, describe and value financial instruments, such as stocks, bonds, derivatives, and currencies. PRD is required for workflows across the entire investment process, including trade execution, portfolio management, risk management, compliance, investment accounting and reporting. There is a tremendous market for this area of focus, including expanding into new clients, as well as competitor replacements.

What You'll Do

Project Planning & Execution:

Serve as the single point of contact for client-facing implementation, migration, and upgrade projects.
Select and adapt the most suitable project management framework for each project.
Develop detailed project plans in collaboration with subject matter experts, aligning with internal and external timelines.
Protect project scope and invoke change management processes when requirements shift.
Proactively identify, assess, and manage project risks along with planning mitigation strategies to ensure successful project delivery.
Lead multi-disciplinary project teams to execute on defined deliverables and business outcomes

Stakeholder Communication

Work alongside sales, product, engineering, implementation and other teams to provide transparency and ensure accountability throughout the implementation process.
Own the project status reporting process, summarizing progress and highlighting blockers and decisions including to senior and executive level audiences.
Facilitate and document internal/external meetings, ensuring engagement and clarity on priorities.
Communicate outcomes and actionable items in a clear, concise manner.

Reporting

Manage project budgets for time and material engagements, keeping stakeholders informed.
Define KPIs and metrics to accurately measure workstream progress.
Create customized reports to summarize project data and visualize key insights.

Organizational Improvement

Create and continuously refine process documentation based on project experience
Serve as an ambassador of Client Engagement Team
Share best practices and mentor junior team members

Required Skills

What We're Looking For

University degree in Data, Business, Technology or other related field
Business fluency in Japanese
A minimum of 9 years of professional experience
Proven experience in project management and process optimization
Genuine interest in data, technology, financial markets
Knowledge of financial products, instruments, and associated metadata
Strong organizational skills to manage multiple projects and identify economies of scale
Experience navigating the organizational structures of financial institutions and an ability to adapt messaging based on audience
Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with diverse teams
Ability to cultivate collaborative and productive relationships
Adaptability and capability to manage multiple priorities

Desired Skills

Experience in financial systems or financial domain knowledge
Experience with Project Management tooling (e.g. Asana, Monday.com, or Jira)
Familiarity with Agile and Hybrid project approaches
PMP or PRINCE2 certification is a plus

Company Overview

FactSet (NYSE:FDS | NASDAQ:FDS) helps the financial community to see more, think bigger, and work better. Our digital platform and enterprise solutions deliver financial data, analytics, and open technology to more than 8,200 global clients, including over 200,000 individual users. Clients across the buy-side and sell-side, as well as wealth managers, private equity firms, and corporations, achieve more every day with our comprehensive and connected content, flexible next-generation workflow solutions, and client-centric specialized support. As a member of the S&P 500, we are committed to sustainable growth and have been recognized among the Best Places to Work in 2023 by Glassdoor as a Glassdoor Employees’ Choice Award winner. Learn more at www.factset.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn.

At FactSet, we celebrate difference of thought, experience, and perspective. Qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to characteristics protected by law.
